questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol dissolve in water to nearly the same extent, while n-pentane is essentially immiscible with water.
Reason (R): The oxygen atom of an ether, like that of an alcohol, can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Ethoxyethane dissolves to about 7.5 g per 100 mL of water and butan-1-ol to about 9 g per 100 mL, whereas pentane barely dissolves.
R is true. The lone pairs on the ether oxygen accept hydrogen bonds from the H atoms of water.
This hydrogen bonding with water is exactly why the ether dissolves like an alcohol of the same mass, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (major alcohol formed):
List-I
(a) Ethanal + CH$_3$MgBr, then hydrolysis
(b) Methanal + C$_2$H$_5$MgBr, then hydrolysis
(c) Propanone + CH$_3$MgBr, then hydrolysis
(d) 2-Methylpropene + $(BH_3)_2$, then $H_2O_2$/NaOH
List-II
(i) Propan-1-ol
(ii) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
(iii) Propan-2-ol
(iv) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
questions.explanation:
(a) An aldehyde other than methanal gives a 2° alcohol: CH$_3$CH(OH)CH$_3$, propan-2-ol, so (iii).
(b) Methanal gives a 1° alcohol: C$_2$H$_5$CH$_2$OH, propan-1-ol, so (i).
(c) A ketone gives a 3° alcohol: (CH$_3$)$_3$COH, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, so (iv).
(d) In hydroboration, boron goes to the CH$_2$ end, giving the anti-Markovnikov product (CH$_3$)$_2$CHCH$_2$OH, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, so (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (main organic product):
List-I
(A) Propan-1-ol + PCC
(B) Propan-1-ol + acidified $KMnO_4$
(C) Propan-2-ol + $CrO_3$
(D) Ethanol + conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 443 K
List-II
(I) Propanone
(II) Ethene
(III) Propanal
(IV) Propanoic acid
questions.explanation:
(A) PCC is a mild reagent that stops at the aldehyde, so propan-1-ol gives propanal (III).
(B) Acidified $KMnO_4$ is a strong oxidant that converts a 1° alcohol directly to the acid, giving propanoic acid (IV).
(C) $CrO_3$ oxidises a 2° alcohol to a ketone, giving propanone (I).
(D) Conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 443 K dehydrates ethanol to ethene (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of tert-butyl alcohol, $(CH_3)_3C-OH$, is:
questions.explanation:
The longest chain containing the carbon that carries –OH has three carbons, so the parent is propane.
The –OH group and a methyl branch are both on C-2, giving 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
2-Methylpropan-1-ol is isobutyl alcohol, a primary alcohol, so it is a different compound.
1,1-Dimethylethanol does not choose the longest chain as the parent.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider all the structurally isomeric alcohols having the molecular formula $C_5H_{12}O$ (ignore stereoisomers). How many of them are primary alcohols?
questions.explanation:
$C_5H_{12}O$ forms 8 structurally isomeric alcohols in total.
Primary (–OH on a $CH_2$ carbon), 4 isomers: pentan-1-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol, 3-methylbutan-1-ol and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol.
Secondary, 3 isomers: pentan-2-ol, pentan-3-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
Tertiary, 1 isomer: 2-methylbutan-2-ol.
The tempting answer 3 comes from overlooking 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol (neopentyl alcohol), which is primary even though its chain is highly branched.
So the number of primary alcohols is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (major product).
List-I
(a) $CH_3CH_2MgBr$ + HCHO, then $H_2O$
(b) $CH_3MgBr$ + $CH_3CHO$, then $H_2O$
(c) $CH_3MgBr$ + $CH_3COCH_3$, then $H_2O$
(d) $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$ + $B_2H_6$, then $H_2O_2$/NaOH
List-II
(i) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
(ii) Propan-1-ol
(iii) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
(iv) Propan-2-ol
questions.explanation:
(a) Ethyl group + HCHO gives $CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$, propan-1-ol (1°). Pair: a-ii.
(b) Methyl group + ethanal gives $CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$, propan-2-ol (2°). Pair: b-iv.
(c) Methyl group + propanone gives $(CH_3)_3COH$, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (3°). Pair: c-i.
(d) In hydroboration, boron goes to the $=CH_2$ carbon, which carries more H. Oxidation gives $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH$, 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Pair: d-iii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When aqueous phenol is treated with bromine water, a white precipitate forms at once. The precipitate is:
questions.explanation:
In water, a polar solvent, the strongly activating –OH group makes all ortho and para positions react with bromine.
Bromine therefore substitutes at C-2, C-4 and C-6, and 2,4,6-tribromophenol separates as a white precipitate.
Monobromophenols (o- and p-) form only in low-polarity solvents such as CS$_2$ or CHCl$_3$ at low temperature, so options (1) and (2) are wrong here.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Methoxybenzene (anisole) is heated with concentrated HI. The products formed are:
questions.explanation:
Alkyl aryl ethers are cleaved at the alkyl–oxygen bond. The aryl–oxygen bond is more stable.
Iodide ion attacks the CH$_3$ carbon of the protonated ether, giving CH$_3$I and phenol.
Phenol does not react further to give iodobenzene. Its sp$^2$ carbon cannot undergo the nucleophilic substitution that this would require.
So iodobenzene, the tempting choice, is never formed.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The C–O–H bond angle in alcohols is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (109°28′). This is mainly because of:
options: repulsion between the two bulky alkyl groups on oxygen
repulsion between the unshared electron pairs on oxygen
sp$^2$ hybridisation of the oxygen atom
partial double bond character of the C–O bond
questions.explanation:
In alcohols, the oxygen is sp$^3$ hybridised and carries two lone pairs.
Lone pair–lone pair repulsion is stronger than bond pair repulsion. It squeezes the C–O–H angle slightly below 109°28′.
Option (a) is the reason ethers show a larger C–O–C angle. An alcohol has only one alkyl group on its oxygen.
Partial double bond character applies to phenol's C–O bond length, not to the bond angle in alcohols.
Answer: (b)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The boiling points of alcohols increase with the number of carbon atoms because of increasing van der Waals forces.
(ii) Among isomeric alcohols, increased branching raises the boiling point.
(iii) Several lower-molecular-mass alcohols are miscible with water in all proportions.
(iv) Pentane is essentially immiscible with water.
(v) Ethers have boiling points comparable to those of alcohols of similar molecular mass.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a larger molecule has stronger van der Waals forces.
(ii) Incorrect: branching reduces surface area, so the boiling point decreases.
(iii) Correct: these alcohols form hydrogen bonds with water.
(iv) Correct: pentane cannot hydrogen bond with water.
(v) Incorrect: ether boiling points resemble those of alkanes and are much lower than those of alcohols.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Vapours of ethanol are passed over heated copper at 573 K. The main organic product is
questions.explanation:
Heated copper at 573 K dehydrogenates primary and secondary alcohols. It removes $H_2$ to form a C=O bond.
Ethanol is a primary alcohol, so $CH_3CH_2OH \rightarrow CH_3CHO + H_2$, giving ethanal.
Only tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration to alkenes over Cu, so ethene is wrong here.
No further oxidation to the acid occurs under these conditions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Pentan-3-one is hydrogenated over finely divided nickel. The product is:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: catalytic hydrogenation (Pt, Pd or Ni) adds H$_2$ across the C=O bond. Aldehydes give primary alcohols, while ketones give secondary alcohols.
CH$_3$CH$_2$COCH$_2$CH$_3$ therefore becomes CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(OH)CH$_2$CH$_3$, which is pentan-3-ol.
The –OH carbon carries two alkyl groups and one H, so the alcohol is secondary, not tertiary.
The carbon skeleton is unchanged, which rules out 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (organic product):
List-I
(A) Propan-1-ol + PCC
(B) Propan-2-ol vapours over heated Cu at 573 K
(C) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol vapours over heated Cu at 573 K
(D) Propan-1-ol + acidified KMnO$_4$
List-II
(i) Propanoic acid
(ii) Propanal
(iii) 2-Methylpropene
(iv) Propanone
questions.explanation:
(A) PCC oxidises a primary alcohol only as far as the aldehyde, giving propanal (ii).
(B) Heated Cu at 573 K dehydrogenates a secondary alcohol to a ketone, giving propanone (iv).
(C) Over hot Cu, a tertiary alcohol undergoes dehydration instead, giving 2-methylpropene (iii).
(D) Acidified KMnO$_4$ is a strong oxidant and converts a primary alcohol directly to propanoic acid (i).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Sodium phenoxide undergoes electrophilic substitution even with carbon dioxide, a weak electrophile, because the phenoxide ion is more reactive than phenol towards electrophiles.
Statement II: In the Reimer–Tiemann reaction, the –CHO group enters mainly at the para position of phenol.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true: the phenoxide ion is even more activated than phenol. It therefore reacts with the weak electrophile CO$_2$ in Kolbe's reaction, giving mainly ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid.
Statement II is false: the Reimer–Tiemann reaction introduces –CHO at the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde, not mainly the para product.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K. What is the main organic product?
options: Ethyl hydrogen sulphate as the final product
questions.explanation:
Ethanol can lose water in two ways depending on temperature.
At 443 K, intramolecular dehydration gives ethene.
At the lower temperature of 413 K, one ethanol molecule attacks a protonated ethanol molecule (SN2), so ethoxyethane is the main product.
Ethanal would need an oxidising agent, which is not present here.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
An alcohol X of molecular formula $C_4H_{10}O$ shows the following behaviour:
(a) With Lucas reagent it gives no turbidity at room temperature.
(b) Its vapours over Cu at 573 K give an aldehyde.
(c) On acid-catalysed dehydration it gives a mixture of alkenes in which but-2-ene is the major product.
X is:
questions.explanation:
(a) No turbidity at room temperature means X is a primary alcohol. This rules out butan-2-ol (2°) and 2-methylpropan-2-ol (3°).
(b) An aldehyde over Cu confirms a primary alcohol. Both butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol remain possible.
(c) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol would give 2-methylpropene, not but-2-ene.
Butan-1-ol gives a mixture of but-1-ene and but-2-ene. But-2-ene is major because the primary carbocation rearranges to a secondary one (NCERT Intext 7.7). So X is butan-1-ol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Using the pK$_a$ values o-nitrophenol 7.2, m-nitrophenol 8.3, p-nitrophenol 7.1, phenol 10.0, m-cresol 10.1 and ethanol 15.9, how many of the following statements are correct?
(i) p-Nitrophenol is a slightly stronger acid than o-nitrophenol.
(ii) m-Cresol is a weaker acid than phenol.
(iii) Phenol is roughly a million times more acidic than ethanol.
(iv) Ethanol is a stronger acid than water.
(v) Sodium ethoxide is a stronger base than sodium hydroxide.
questions.explanation:
A lower pK$_a$ means a stronger acid.
(i) Correct: 7.1 < 7.2.
(ii) Correct: 10.1 > 10.0, because the electron-releasing CH$_3$ group lowers acidity.
(iii) Correct: the pK$_a$ values differ by about 6 units, which is about $10^6$ in acid strength.
(iv) Incorrect: alcohols are weaker acids than water.
(v) Correct: an alkoxide ion is a better proton acceptor than OH$^-$.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the physical properties of phenols is INCORRECT?
options: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile because of intramolecular hydrogen bonding
p-Nitrophenol is less volatile because its molecules associate through intermolecular hydrogen bonds
o-Nitrophenol is more soluble in water than p-nitrophenol because its –OH group is freely available for hydrogen bonding with water
Phenol boils at a much higher temperature than toluene of comparable molecular mass because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in o-nitrophenol the –OH group hydrogen bonds to the neighbouring –NO$_2$ group within the same molecule, so the molecules do not associate.
(2) Correct: in p-nitrophenol, intermolecular hydrogen bonding associates the molecules, so the boiling point is higher.
(3) Incorrect: the –OH of the ortho isomer is tied up internally, which makes it less available to hydrogen bond with water. o-Nitrophenol is therefore the less soluble isomer.
(4) Correct: phenol's –OH forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which toluene lacks.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle because of repulsive interaction between the two bulky alkyl groups.
Statement II: In ethers, the two bond pairs and two lone pairs on oxygen are arranged in an approximately trigonal planar manner.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The two bulky R groups repel each other, which opens the C–O–C angle slightly beyond 109°28′.
Statement II is incorrect. Four electron pairs (2 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs) around oxygen are arranged approximately tetrahedrally, not trigonal planar.
Answer: (b)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An alcohol is esterified with an acid chloride, $ROH + R'COCl \rightarrow R'COOR + HCl$. Why is pyridine added to the reaction mixture?
options: To act as a dehydrating agent that removes the water formed
To neutralise the HCl formed, which shifts the equilibrium towards the ester
To protonate the alcohol so that it becomes a better electrophile
To oxidise the alcohol before esterification
questions.explanation:
Esterification with an acid chloride releases HCl, not water.
Pyridine is a base. It neutralises the HCl as soon as it forms, which pushes the equilibrium to the right and raises the ester yield.
Removing water (option 1) applies to esterification with carboxylic acids or anhydrides, where conc. $H_2SO_4$ is used.
Pyridine does not protonate or oxidise the alcohol.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (main organic product).
List-I:
(a) Kolbe's reaction of sodium phenoxide with CO$_2$, then acidification
(b) Phenol with CHCl$_3$ and aqueous NaOH, then hydrolysis
(c) Cumene hydroperoxide treated with dilute acid
(d) Phenol heated with zinc dust
List-II:
(i) Benzene
(ii) Phenol and propanone
(iii) 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid
(iv) Salicylaldehyde
questions.explanation:
(a) Kolbe's reaction: the phenoxide ion is attacked by the weak electrophile CO$_2$, giving ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid). So (a)-(iii).
(b) Reimer–Tiemann reaction: a –CHO group is introduced at the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde. So (b)-(iv).
(c) Acid treatment of cumene hydroperoxide gives phenol, with acetone (propanone) as a by-product. So (c)-(ii).
(d) Zinc dust converts phenol to benzene. So (d)-(i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cumene is oxidised by air and the product is treated with dilute acid to give phenol and a by-product X. X is treated with methylmagnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis to give Y. The vapours of Y are passed over heated copper at 573 K to give Z. Z is:
questions.explanation:
The cumene process gives phenol plus acetone, so X = propanone.
A ketone with a Grignard reagent gives a tertiary alcohol. $CH_3MgBr$ + propanone, then hydrolysis, gives Y = 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
Over Cu at 573 K, primary and secondary alcohols are dehydrogenated. Tertiary alcohols instead undergo dehydration.
So Z = 2-methylpropene.
Options (1) and (2) wrongly assume dehydrogenation of Y.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following give a secondary alcohol as the major product?
(i) Propanone + NaBH$_4$
(ii) Ethanal + CH$_3$MgBr, then hydrolysis
(iii) Methanal + C$_2$H$_5$MgBr, then hydrolysis
(iv) Propanoic acid + LiAlH$_4$, then H$_2$O
(v) Propene + H$_2$O in presence of H$^+$
(vi) Propene + $(BH_3)_2$, then $H_2O_2$/NaOH
(vii) Butan-2-one + H$_2$/Ni
questions.explanation:
(i) A ketone is reduced to propan-2-ol: 2°.
(ii) An aldehyde other than HCHO with a Grignard reagent gives propan-2-ol: 2°.
(iii) Methanal with a Grignard reagent gives propan-1-ol: 1°.
(iv) An acid with LiAlH$_4$ gives propan-1-ol: 1°.
(v) Markovnikov hydration gives propan-2-ol: 2°.
(vi) Hydroboration–oxidation gives propan-1-ol: 1°.
(vii) A ketone is reduced to butan-2-ol: 2°.
The secondary alcohols come from (i), (ii), (v) and (vii), so the count is 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the cleavage of ethers by hydrogen halides are correct?
(i) The first step is protonation of the ether oxygen to form an oxonium ion.
(ii) Dialkyl ethers are readily cleaved by dilute HCl at room temperature.
(iii) For a mixed ether having primary/secondary alkyl groups, iodide ion attacks the less substituted carbon of the oxonium ion by S$_N$2 mechanism.
(iv) Ethoxyethane with excess HI at high temperature finally gives two molecules of ethyl iodide.
(v) The phenol formed from anisole and HI reacts further with HI to give iodobenzene.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the ether is first protonated to an oxonium ion.
(ii) Incorrect: cleavage needs drastic conditions, such as concentrated HI or HBr at high temperature. HCl is the least reactive halide acid.
(iii) Correct: the S$_N$2 attack occurs at the less substituted carbon, so the lower alkyl group becomes the iodide.
(iv) Correct: the ethanol formed reacts with more HI to give C$_2$H$_5$I.
(v) Incorrect: the sp$^2$ carbon of phenol does not undergo nucleophilic substitution.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are allylic alcohols?
(i) CH$_2$=CH–CH$_2$OH
(ii) CH$_2$=CH–OH
(iii) CH$_2$=CH–CH(OH)–CH$_3$
(iv) CH$_3$–CH=CH–CH$_2$OH
(v) C$_6$H$_5$–CH$_2$OH
(vi) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol
questions.explanation:
An allylic alcohol has its –OH on an sp$^3$ carbon directly next to a C=C bond.
(i) Allylic (primary).
(ii) Not allylic: the –OH is on the sp$^2$ carbon itself, so it is vinylic.
(iii) Allylic (secondary).
(iv) Allylic (primary).
(v) Not allylic: the –OH carbon is next to an aromatic ring, so it is benzylic.
(vi) Allylic: C-1 bearing –OH is adjacent to the C2=C3 double bond.
This gives 4 allylic alcohols.
Answer: (c)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol dissolve in water to nearly the same extent (about 7.5 g and 9 g per 100 mL respectively), whereas n-pentane is practically immiscible.
Reason (R): Like the oxygen of an alcohol, the oxygen atom of an ether can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT reports 7.5 g (ethoxyethane) and 9 g (butan-1-ol) per 100 mL of water, while pentane is essentially immiscible.
R is true: the lone pairs on the ether oxygen accept hydrogen bonds from the H atoms of water.
R is also the reason for A. Hydrogen bonding with water makes ethers about as soluble as alcohols of the same molecular mass.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the common names in List-I with the IUPAC names in List-II.
List-I
(a) Isobutyl alcohol
(b) tert-Butyl alcohol
(c) Resorcinol
(d) Glycerol
List-II
(i) Benzene-1,3-diol
(ii) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
(iii) Propane-1,2,3-triol
(iv) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
questions.explanation:
(a) Isobutyl alcohol is $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH$. The –OH is on C-1 and the methyl is on C-2, so it is 2-methylpropan-1-ol, matching (iv).
(b) tert-Butyl alcohol is $(CH_3)_3COH$. The –OH and the methyl are both on C-2, so it is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, matching (ii).
(c) Resorcinol is the 1,3-dihydroxybenzene, i.e. benzene-1,3-diol, matching (i). Catechol is the 1,2-isomer.
(d) Glycerol is $HOCH_2CH(OH)CH_2OH$, i.e. propane-1,2,3-triol, matching (iii). The 'e' of propane is retained before 'triol'.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: When anisole is heated with HI, the products are phenol and methyl iodide, not iodobenzene and methanol.
Statement II: The O–C$_6$H$_5$ bond is stronger than the O–CH$_3$ bond, because the phenyl carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised and the O–C$_6$H$_5$ bond has partial double bond character.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. HI protonates the ether oxygen. I$^-$ then attacks the methyl carbon and breaks the O–CH$_3$ bond, giving CH$_3$I and phenol.
Statement II is true. The aryl–oxygen bond is stronger because the phenyl carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised and the bond has partial double bond character.
Phenol does not react further to give a halide, since its sp$^2$ carbon cannot undergo nucleophilic substitution.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the physical properties of ethers is INCORRECT?
options: The C–O bonds in ethers are polar, so ethers have a net dipole moment.
Boiling points of ethers are comparable to those of alkanes of similar molecular mass.
Ethers have boiling points much higher than alcohols of similar molecular mass because of their dipole moment.
The oxygen atom of an ether can accept hydrogen bonds from water molecules.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the C–O bonds are polar and the molecule is bent, so ethers have a net dipole moment.
(2) Correct: ethoxyethane boils at 307.6 K, close to n-pentane at 309.1 K.
(3) Incorrect: the weak polarity of ethers barely affects boiling point. Alcohols such as butan-1-ol (390 K) boil much higher because they form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
(4) Correct: the ether oxygen accepts hydrogen bonds from water, which explains their solubility.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is treated with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide, and the intermediate is then hydrolysed. What is the main product and the name of this reaction?
questions.explanation:
CHCl$_3$/NaOH introduces a –CHO group at the ortho position of phenol. This is the Reimer–Tiemann reaction.
The substituted benzal chloride intermediate is hydrolysed by alkali to give salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).
Kolbe's reaction uses CO$_2$ and gives salicylic acid, so option (1) is wrong.
Benzaldehyde cannot be the product because the –OH group is retained.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In phenol, the –OH group is attached to an $sp^2$ hybridised carbon. How does this feature make phenol ionise more readily than an alcohol?
options: The $sp^2$ carbon releases electrons to oxygen, which strengthens the O–H bond.
The more electronegative $sp^2$ carbon lowers the electron density on oxygen, which increases the polarity of the O–H bond.
The $sp^2$ carbon makes the C–O bond longer than in methanol.
The $sp^2$ carbon places a full negative charge on the oxygen of phenol.
questions.explanation:
An $sp^2$ carbon is more electronegative than an $sp^3$ carbon.
It pulls electron density away from oxygen, so the O–H bond becomes more polar and ionises more easily.
Option (1) is wrong because electron release would decrease acidity.
Option (3) is wrong because the C–O bond in phenol (136 pm) is actually shorter than in methanol.
Option (4) is wrong because the resonance structures put a positive charge on the oxygen of phenol.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Anisole is treated with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric acid and concentrated nitric acid. The product obtained is:
questions.explanation:
Nitration is an electrophilic substitution on the ring. The –OCH$_3$ group activates the ring and directs to ortho and para positions, as –OH does in phenol.
Therefore a mixture of ortho- and para-nitroanisole is formed.
The meta isomer is not the major product. The ether C–O bond is not cleaved by the nitrating mixture, so methanol is not released.
Picric acid is the product of phenol, not anisole.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The ether $CH_3CH_2CH_2-O-CH(CH_3)-CH_2CH_3$ is correctly named in the IUPAC system as:
questions.explanation:
The two groups on oxygen are propyl (3 C) and sec-butyl (4 C).
The larger group, butane, becomes the parent, and $C_3H_7O-$ is written as the propoxy substituent.
The oxygen is attached to the second carbon of the butane chain. Numbering from the nearer end gives locant 2, not 3.
So the name is 2-propoxybutane. Option (1) wrongly takes the smaller group as the parent, and option (4) is a common name.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Commercial alcohol is made unfit for drinking by 'denaturation'. Which pair of substances is added for this purpose, as described in NCERT?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that commercial ethanol is denatured by adding two substances.
Copper sulphate gives the alcohol a colour.
Pyridine is a foul-smelling liquid that makes it undrinkable.
Other additives such as methanol are sometimes used in practice, but the pair given in NCERT is CuSO$_4$ with pyridine.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent/condition acting on phenol) with List-II (main organic product):
List-I
(A) CHCl$_3$ + aq. NaOH, then acidification
(B) Heating with zinc dust
(C) Chromic acid
(D) Br$_2$ in CS$_2$ at low temperature
List-II
(I) Benzene
(II) Benzoquinone
(III) Salicylaldehyde
(IV) Mixture of o- and p-bromophenol
questions.explanation:
(A) Reimer–Tiemann reaction: a –CHO group enters the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde (III).
(B) Heating phenol with zinc dust removes the oxygen and gives benzene (I).
(C) Chromic acid oxidises phenol to benzoquinone, a conjugated diketone (II).
(D) Bromine in a low-polarity solvent at low temperature gives monobromophenols, the o- and p- isomers (IV).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one of the following compounds reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form a sodium salt and water?
questions.explanation:
Phenol is acidic enough to give up its proton to aqueous NaOH. It forms sodium phenoxide and water.
Alcohols such as ethanol and propan-2-ol are weaker acids than water. They form alkoxides only with active metals like Na or K, not with aqueous NaOH.
Methoxybenzene (anisole) has no O–H bond, so it cannot act as an acid here.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alcohols is the least soluble in water?
questions.explanation:
Alcohols dissolve in water because their –OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
The alkyl part of the molecule is hydrophobic. As it grows larger, solubility decreases.
Methanol, ethanol and propan-1-ol are miscible with water in all proportions.
Pentan-1-ol has the largest hydrophobic chain of the four, so it is the least soluble.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction/test) with List-II (product/reagent).
List-I:
(A) Reimer–Tiemann reaction
(B) Kolbe's reaction
(C) Cumene process
(D) Lucas test
List-II:
(i) Phenol and acetone
(ii) Salicylaldehyde
(iii) ortho-Hydroxybenzoic acid
(iv) Conc. HCl + anhydrous $ZnCl_2$
questions.explanation:
A: Phenol reacts with $CHCl_3$ and NaOH. A –CHO group enters the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde. So A-(ii).
B: Phenoxide reacts with $CO_2$ to give ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid. So B-(iii).
C: Cumene hydroperoxide is treated with dilute acid, giving phenol and acetone. So C-(i).
D: Lucas reagent is conc. HCl with $ZnCl_2$. So D-(iv).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aromatic hydrocarbon X ($C_9H_{12}$) is oxidised by air and the product is treated with dilute acid. This gives phenol and a compound Y. Y is treated with methylmagnesium bromide, and the adduct is hydrolysed to give Z. What is Z?
questions.explanation:
X ($C_9H_{12}$) is cumene. Air oxidation gives cumene hydroperoxide, and dilute acid converts it to phenol and Y.
So Y is acetone (propanone), $CH_3COCH_3$, which is a ketone.
A Grignard reagent adds to a ketone, and hydrolysis gives a tertiary alcohol.
$CH_3MgBr$ + $CH_3COCH_3$, then hydrolysis, gives $(CH_3)_3COH$. This is 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
Propan-2-ol would come from reducing acetone, not from a Grignard reaction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is obtained from chlorobenzene by fusing it with NaOH and then acidifying. The conditions used for the fusion step are:
questions.explanation:
The C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene is very hard to break, so drastic conditions are needed.
Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm. This gives sodium phenoxide, which is acidified to phenol.
443 K is the temperature for dehydrating ethanol to ethene.
273–278 K is the temperature range for diazotisation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate method to prepare tert-butyl ethyl ether, $(CH_3)_3C–O–C_2H_5$?
options: Heating a mixture of ethanol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol with conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 413 K
questions.explanation:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by $S_N2$ attack of an alkoxide on an alkyl halide. It works best with a primary alkyl halide.
(1): ethoxide is also a strong base. With a tertiary halide it causes elimination, giving 2-methylpropene.
(2) and (3): acid dehydration with a tertiary alcohol or halide favours alkene formation over ether.
(4): the bulky group is in the alkoxide and the halide is primary, so substitution gives the ether.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane, (CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–CH$_3$, reacts with HI to give methyl iodide and tert-butyl alcohol.
Statement II: In this reaction, the protonated ether loses a methanol molecule in the slow step to form a tert-butyl carbocation, i.e., the reaction follows the S$_N$1 pathway.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement II is correct. After protonation, the C–O bond to the tert-butyl group breaks in the slow step. This releases CH$_3$OH and gives the stable (CH$_3$)$_3$C$^+$ ion, so the reaction is S$_N$1.
I$^-$ then combines with this carbocation in the fast step.
Statement I is therefore incorrect. The actual products are tert-butyl iodide and methanol, not methyl iodide and tert-butyl alcohol.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In Kolbe's reaction, carbon dioxide (a weak electrophile) substitutes into the ring of which species, and what is the main product?
questions.explanation:
Treating phenol with NaOH gives the phenoxide ion, which is even more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic aromatic substitution.
Because it is so reactive, phenoxide can react with CO$_2$, which is only a weak electrophile.
The main product is ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid), not the para isomer.
The ring keeps its –OH group, so plain benzoic acid is not formed.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: m-Nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol but less acidic than p-nitrophenol.
Statement II: A nitro group at the meta position cannot take part in delocalising the negative charge of the phenoxide ion through resonance, whereas at ortho and para positions it can.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: the pKa values are p-nitrophenol 7.1, m-nitrophenol 8.3 and phenol 10.0.
Statement II is correct: NCERT says the acid-strengthening effect of –$NO_2$ is more pronounced at ortho and para positions. This is because the phenoxide charge can be delocalised effectively onto the nitro group only from those positions.
At the meta position, –$NO_2$ still withdraws electrons, so acidity rises, but only to a smaller extent.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the cleavage of ethers by hydrogen halides are correct?
(i) Anisole with HI gives phenol and methyl iodide.
(ii) Anisole with HI gives iodobenzene and methanol.
(iii) 1-Methoxypropane with one equivalent of HI gives methyl iodide and propan-1-ol.
(iv) 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane with HI gives methanol and 2-iodo-2-methylpropane by an SN1 pathway.
(v) With excess HI at high temperature, ethoxyethane finally gives two molecules of ethyl iodide.
(vi) HCl is more reactive than HI for cleaving ethers.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the O–$CH_3$ bond breaks because the O–aryl bond has partial double bond character.
(ii) Incorrect: an $sp^2$ ring carbon does not undergo nucleophilic substitution, so iodobenzene does not form.
(iii) Correct: with primary/secondary groups, $I^-$ attacks the lower (less substituted) alkyl group by SN2.
(iv) Correct: the stable $(CH_3)_3C^+$ forms, so the halide is tertiary (SN1).
(v) Correct: the ethanol first formed reacts with more HI to give $C_2H_5I$.
(vi) Incorrect: the reactivity order is HI > HBr > HCl.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the product formed when phenol is heated with zinc dust?
questions.explanation:
Heating phenol with zinc dust removes the oxygen and converts phenol to benzene.
This is the only reaction in which phenol undergoes C–O bond cleavage.
Cyclohexanol would need ring hydrogenation.
Benzoquinone is an oxidation product formed with chromic acid, not with zinc.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the compounds:
(P) C$_6$H$_5$–CH(OH)–CH$_3$
(Q) CH$_2$=CH–C(CH$_3$)$_2$–OH
(R) C$_6$H$_5$–OH
(S) CH$_2$=C(OH)–CH$_3$
Which option classifies all four correctly?
options: P: secondary benzylic; Q: tertiary allylic; R: C$_{sp^2}$–OH compound; S: vinylic alcohol
P: primary benzylic; Q: tertiary vinylic; R: C$_{sp^3}$–OH compound; S: allylic alcohol
P: secondary benzylic; Q: secondary allylic; R: C$_{sp^2}$–OH compound; S: allylic alcohol
P: secondary allylic; Q: tertiary allylic; R: benzylic alcohol; S: vinylic alcohol
questions.explanation:
(P) The –OH carbon is sp$^3$, lies next to the benzene ring and carries two carbon groups. It is a secondary benzylic alcohol.
(Q) The –OH carbon is sp$^3$, adjacent to C=C and bonded to three carbons. It is a tertiary allylic alcohol, since allylic alcohols can be 1°, 2° or 3°.
(R) In phenol, the –OH is on an sp$^2$ aryl carbon, giving a C$_{sp^2}$–OH bond.
(S) The –OH is on a doubly bonded carbon, so it is vinylic.
Only option (a) gets all four right.
Answer: (a)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pKa of phenol is 10.0 and that of p-nitrophenol is 7.1. Approximately how many times larger is the acid dissociation constant ($K_a$) of p-nitrophenol than that of phenol? (Use $10^{0.9} \approx 7.94$)
questions.explanation:
Given: pKa (phenol) = 10.0 and pKa (p-nitrophenol) = 7.1.
Formula: $K_a = 10^{-pK_a}$, so the ratio is $10^{(10.0-7.1)}$.
Substituting: $10^{2.9} = 10^{2} \times 10^{0.9} = 100 \times 7.94$.
So the ratio ≈ 794.
The value 2.9 is the pKa difference, not the ratio, and 1.41 wrongly divides the pKa values.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Ethyl methyl ether cannot be conveniently prepared by heating a mixture of methanol and ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K.
Statement II: Under these conditions, either protonated alcohol can be attacked by either alcohol molecule, so a mixture of methoxymethane, ethoxyethane and ethyl methyl ether is formed.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, and Statement II explains Statement I
Both statements are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Ether formation here is an SN2 attack of an alcohol on a protonated alcohol.
With both alcohols present, four combinations are possible: CH₃OH on protonated CH₃OH, C₂H₅OH on protonated C₂H₅OH, and the two cross combinations.
These give three ethers: CH₃OCH₃, C₂H₅OC₂H₅ and CH₃OC₂H₅. The desired unsymmetrical ether is therefore obtained only as part of a mixture.
So Statement I is correct, Statement II is correct, and Statement II explains Statement I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the following isomeric alcohols of formula $C_4H_{10}O$, which has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation:
All four isomers have the same molar mass and can all form hydrogen bonds.
The deciding factor is branching. More branching makes the molecule more compact, which reduces surface area and weakens van der Waals forces.
Butan-1-ol is the unbranched (straight-chain) isomer, so it has the highest boiling point.
2-Methylpropan-2-ol is the most branched, so it has the lowest boiling point.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Anisole is treated with bromine in ethanoic acid without any iron(III) bromide catalyst. The major product is:
questions.explanation:
The –OCH$_3$ group strongly activates the benzene ring. Bromination therefore occurs even without a Lewis acid such as FeBr$_3$.
The methoxy group is ortho/para directing, so the meta product (3-bromoanisole) is not the major product.
The para isomer, 4-bromoanisole, forms in about 90% yield. It is favoured over the ortho isomer.
Bromobenzene would require loss of the methoxy group, which does not occur.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Phenol is a much stronger acid than ethanol.
Reason (R): In phenoxide ion the negative charge is delocalised over the benzene ring, whereas in ethoxide ion it is localised on oxygen.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true: the pKa of phenol is 10.0 and that of ethanol is 15.9, so phenol is roughly a million times more acidic.
R is true: the negative charge of phenoxide spreads over the ring through resonance, while the charge in an alkoxide stays on oxygen.
Delocalisation stabilises the conjugate base and favours ionisation, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction of phenol) with List-II (main product):
List-I
(A) Sodium phenoxide + CO$_2$, then acidification
(B) CHCl$_3$ + aq. NaOH, then hydrolysis
(C) Br$_2$ in CS$_2$ at low temperature
(D) Chromic acid
List-II
(I) Benzoquinone
(II) o-Hydroxybenzoic acid
(III) o- and p-Bromophenol
(IV) Salicylaldehyde
questions.explanation:
(A) Kolbe's reaction: phenoxide reacts with CO$_2$ to give o-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid), so A-II.
(B) Reimer–Tiemann reaction: CHCl$_3$/NaOH gives salicylaldehyde, so B-IV.
(C) In a solvent of low polarity at low temperature, only monobromination occurs, giving o- and p-bromophenol, so C-III.
(D) Chromic acid oxidises phenol to benzoquinone, so D-I.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are unsymmetrical (mixed) ethers?
C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$, C$_2$H$_5$OCH$_3$, C$_2$H$_5$OC$_6$H$_5$, CH$_3$OCH$_3$, C$_6$H$_5$OCH$_3$, CH$_3$OCH(CH$_3$)$_2$
questions.explanation:
An ether is symmetrical if both groups on oxygen are the same. It is unsymmetrical (mixed) if the two groups differ.
Symmetrical: C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$ and CH$_3$OCH$_3$.
Unsymmetrical: C$_2$H$_5$OCH$_3$ (ethyl, methyl), C$_2$H$_5$OC$_6$H$_5$ (ethyl, phenyl), C$_6$H$_5$OCH$_3$ (phenyl, methyl) and CH$_3$OCH(CH$_3$)$_2$ (methyl, isopropyl).
So the count of unsymmetrical ethers is 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following combinations give a tertiary alcohol after hydrolysis of the adduct?
(i) CH$_3$MgBr + propanone
(ii) CH$_3$MgBr + ethanal
(iii) C$_2$H$_5$MgBr + methanal
(iv) C$_2$H$_5$MgBr + butanone
(v) C$_6$H$_5$MgBr + propanone
questions.explanation:
Rule: a Grignard reagent gives a primary alcohol with methanal, a secondary alcohol with other aldehydes, and a tertiary alcohol with ketones.
(i) Ketone, so tertiary: 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
(ii) Aldehyde other than methanal, so secondary: propan-2-ol.
(iii) Methanal, so primary: propan-1-ol.
(iv) Ketone, so tertiary: 3-methylpentan-3-ol.
(v) Ketone, so tertiary: 2-phenylpropan-2-ol.
Combinations (i), (iv) and (v) give tertiary alcohols, so the count is 3.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Bromination of anisole with $Br_2$ in ethanoic acid requires $FeBr_3$ as catalyst.
(ii) The major product of bromination of anisole in ethanoic acid is the para isomer, formed in about 90% yield.
(iii) 1-Methoxypropane on heating with HBr gives bromomethane and propan-1-ol.
(iv) With excess HI, the phenol formed from anisole is further converted to iodobenzene.
(v) Anisole reacts with $CH_3COCl$ in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ to give ortho and para methoxyacetophenones.
(vi) Nitration of anisole with concentrated $HNO_3$ and $H_2SO_4$ gives mainly m-nitroanisole.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: –OCH3 activates the ring, so no Lewis acid catalyst is needed.
(ii) Correct: p-bromoanisole is formed in about 90% yield.
(iii) Correct: with primary alkyl groups, the attack is $S_N2$ and the lower alkyl group forms the halide, giving CH3Br and CH3CH2CH2OH.
(iv) Incorrect: the $sp^2$ carbon of phenol resists nucleophilic substitution, so no iodobenzene forms.
(v) Correct: this is Friedel–Crafts acylation at the ortho and para positions.
(vi) Incorrect: –OCH3 is ortho, para directing, so o- and p-nitroanisole form.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol was first isolated in the early nineteenth century. Which option correctly gives its other common name and its original source?
options: Wood spirit; destructive distillation of wood
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that phenol is also called carbolic acid and was first isolated from coal tar. Today it is produced synthetically.
Wood spirit is methanol, which was made by destructive distillation of wood.
Picric acid is 2,4,6-trinitrophenol.
Molasses is a source of sugar for making ethanol by fermentation.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Tertiary alcohols are dehydrated by acids under milder conditions than primary alcohols.
Reason (R): Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation with mild oxidising agents.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The ease of dehydration follows the order tertiary > secondary > primary.
R is also true. A tertiary alcohol has no H atom on the carbinol carbon, so mild reagents do not oxidise it.
However, R does not explain A. Dehydration is easier because the rate-determining step forms a carbocation, and the tertiary carbocation is the most stable. Resistance to oxidation has nothing to do with this.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the cumene process, 470 g of phenol is obtained. What mass of acetone is formed along with it? (Molar masses: phenol = 94 g/mol, acetone = 58 g/mol; 1 mol of cumene hydroperoxide gives 1 mol each of phenol and acetone.)
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of phenol = 470 g, M(phenol) = 94 g/mol, M(acetone) = 58 g/mol.
Formula: moles of acetone = moles of phenol, because they are formed in a 1:1 ratio.
Substituting: moles of phenol = 470/94 = 5 mol, so moles of acetone = 5 mol.
Mass of acetone = 5 × 58 = 290 g.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which combination of reactants is most suitable for preparing tert-butyl ethyl ether (2-ethoxy-2-methylpropane) by Williamson synthesis?
questions.explanation:
Williamson synthesis works best when the alkyl halide is primary, because the reaction is SN2.
In option (2), the bulky tert-butyl group is carried by the alkoxide and the halide is primary (bromoethane), so SN2 succeeds and the ether forms.
Option (1) uses a tertiary halide, so the ethoxide acts as a base and 2-methylprop-1-ene forms.
Option (3) fails because a tertiary alcohol readily gives an alkene under acid dehydration.
Option (4) gives a different ether, 1-ethoxy-2-methylpropane.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the sequence:
Phenol $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) NaOH (ii) CO}_2\text{, pressure (iii) H}^+}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{(CH}_3\text{CO)}_2\text{O, conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ (trace)}}$ Q
Which of the following correctly identifies Q and one of its properties?
options: Q is phenyl ethanoate, used as a flavouring ester
Q is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, which gives a white precipitate with bromine water
Q is methyl salicylate, an analgesic oil
Q is acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin), which has analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic properties
questions.explanation:
Step 1: NaOH converts phenol to sodium phenoxide. Kolbe's reaction with CO$_2$, followed by acidification, gives o-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) = P.
Step 2: Acetic anhydride with a trace of conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ acetylates the phenolic –OH of P.
Acetylation of salicylic acid gives aspirin = Q, which NCERT describes as analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic.
Phenyl ethanoate would form only if phenol itself were acetylated, without the Kolbe step.
Methyl salicylate would need methanol, which is absent here.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: A Grignard reagent reacts with methanal, and the adduct is hydrolysed, to give a primary alcohol.
Statement II: A Grignard reagent reacts with a ketone, and the adduct is hydrolysed, to give a secondary alcohol.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. Methanal (HCHO) has two H atoms on its carbonyl carbon. Adding R from RMgX gives RCH$_2$OH, a primary alcohol.
Statement II is false. A ketone already carries two alkyl groups on its carbonyl carbon. Adding a third R group gives a tertiary alcohol.
Secondary alcohols come from aldehydes other than methanal.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the Williamson synthesis of ethers, an alkyl halide reacts with a sodium alkoxide. By which mechanism does the alkoxide ion attack the alkyl halide?
questions.explanation:
In Williamson synthesis, R–X + R'O⁻Na⁺ gives R–O–R' + NaX.
The alkoxide ion is a strong nucleophile. It attacks the carbon bearing the halogen from the back side in a single step, which is an SN2 reaction.
This is why primary alkyl halides work best.
An SN1 pathway with hindered halides would instead allow elimination to dominate.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Anisole on heating with HI gives phenol and methyl iodide, not iodobenzene and methanol.
Reason (R): The O–C$_6$H$_5$ bond is stronger than the O–CH$_3$ bond because the phenyl carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised and the bond has partial double bond character.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Anisole is protonated to a methylphenyl oxonium ion, and I$^-$ then breaks the O–CH$_3$ bond, giving CH$_3$I and phenol.
R is true. The sp$^2$ carbon of the ring and the conjugation of the oxygen lone pair give the O–C$_6$H$_5$ bond partial double bond character, which strengthens it.
Because the weaker O–CH$_3$ bond is the one broken, R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the decreasing order of acid strength of alcohols?
questions.explanation:
Alkyl groups such as –CH3 and –C2H5 are electron-releasing.
They raise the electron density on oxygen and lower the polarity of the O–H bond, which makes it harder to release H⁺.
A tertiary alcohol has the most alkyl groups on the carbinol carbon, so it is the weakest acid. A primary alcohol has the fewest, so it is the strongest.
Order: 1° > 2° > 3°. The order 3° > 2° > 1° is the dehydration order, which is a common confusion.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Propene is converted to compound A by hydroboration–oxidation (B$_2$H$_6$, then H$_2$O$_2$/aqueous NaOH). A is oxidised with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) to B. B is treated with CH$_3$MgBr and the adduct is hydrolysed to give C. What is C?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In hydroboration–oxidation, boron adds to the carbon carrying more hydrogens. The result is anti-Markovnikov addition of water, so A is propan-1-ol.
Step 2: PCC oxidises a primary alcohol only as far as the aldehyde, so B is propanal (CH$_3$CH$_2$CHO).
Step 3: CH$_3$MgBr adds to this aldehyde, and hydrolysis gives a secondary alcohol, CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(OH)CH$_3$. So C is butan-2-ol.
Why not 2-methylpropan-2-ol: that product would require acid-catalysed (Markovnikov) hydration of propene, giving propan-2-ol, then oxidation to propanone.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (boiling point):
List-I
(A) Methanol
(B) Ethanol
(C) Butan-1-ol
(D) Ethoxyethane
List-II
(I) 307.6 K
(II) 337 K
(III) 351 K
(IV) 390 K
questions.explanation:
Ethoxyethane has no intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so it has the lowest value: D-I (307.6 K).
Among the alcohols, boiling point rises with the number of carbon atoms.
So methanol is A-II (337 K), ethanol is B-III (351 K) and butan-1-ol is C-IV (390 K).
Note that butan-1-ol and ethoxyethane are isomers ($C_4H_{10}O$), yet they differ by about 82 K because of hydrogen bonding.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The carbon–oxygen bond length in phenol is slightly less than that in methanol.
Reason (R): In phenol, the –OH group is attached to an sp$^3$ hybridised carbon, and its C–O sigma bond is formed by sp$^3$–sp$^3$ overlap exactly as in methanol.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The phenol C–O bond (136 pm) is shorter than the methanol C–O bond.
R is false. In phenol, the –OH is attached to an sp$^2$ hybridised ring carbon. The oxygen lone pair is also conjugated with the ring, which gives the C–O bond partial double bond character.
These two factors explain the shorter bond. If the bonding were identical to methanol, as R claims, the lengths would be nearly equal.
Answer: (c)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Exactly three monohydric phenols have the molecular formula $C_7H_8O$; their IUPAC names are 2-methylphenol, 3-methylphenol and 4-methylphenol.
Statement II: Methoxybenzene and phenylmethanol are also isomers of formula $C_7H_8O$, but neither of them is a phenol.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. A $C_7H_8O$ phenol must be a methylphenol, and only the o-, m- and p- positions are possible. These give the three cresols.
Statement II is correct. Anisole ($C_6H_5OCH_3$) is an ether.
Benzyl alcohol ($C_6H_5CH_2OH$) has its –OH on an $sp^3$ carbon, so it is a benzylic alcohol, not a phenol.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenetole is the common name of $C_6H_5OCH_2CH_3$. Its IUPAC name is:
questions.explanation:
In IUPAC naming, an ether is treated as a hydrocarbon in which one H is replaced by an –OR group. The larger group becomes the parent.
Phenyl (6 C) is larger than ethyl (2 C), so benzene is the parent and $-OC_2H_5$ is the ethoxy substituent: ethoxybenzene.
Methoxybenzene is anisole.
Ethyl phenyl ether is the common name, not the IUPAC name.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Arrange the following in increasing order of boiling point:
P: Butan-1-ol
Q: n-Pentane
R: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
S: Ethoxyethane
T: Butan-2-ol
questions.explanation:
Ethoxyethane (307.6 K) and n-pentane (309.1 K) have no intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so they come first, with the ether slightly lower: S < Q.
The three butanols are isomers that all hydrogen bond, so branching decides their order.
The tertiary alcohol R is the most branched, so it boils lowest of the three. Butan-2-ol T is next, and unbranched butan-1-ol P (390 K) is the highest.
This gives S < Q < R < T < P.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Most of the phenol produced worldwide is manufactured by a process that also gives acetone in large quantities as a by-product. The starting hydrocarbon in this process is:
questions.explanation:
Most of the world's phenol is made from cumene.
Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide. Dilute acid then converts this to phenol and acetone.
Chlorobenzene, benzenesulphonic acid and aniline are laboratory routes. None of them gives acetone.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Acid-catalysed hydration of 1-methylcyclohexene gives a tertiary alcohol as the major product, whereas its hydroboration–oxidation gives a secondary alcohol.
Statement II: In hydroboration, the boron atom attaches to the $sp^2$ carbon carrying the greater number of hydrogen atoms, and it is later replaced by –OH.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
In 1-methylcyclohexene, C-1 carries the $CH_3$ group and no H; C-2 carries one H.
Acid hydration: protonation at C-2 gives a 3° carbocation at C-1. Water attacks there, giving 1-methylcyclohexanol (3°).
Hydroboration: boron goes to C-2, the carbon with more H. Oxidation replaces B with OH, giving 2-methylcyclohexanol (2°).
So Statement I is true.
Statement II is exactly the NCERT rule for hydroboration, so it is also true. It explains why the two methods give different alcohols.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: When 1-methylcyclohexene undergoes acid-catalysed hydration, the major product is 1-methylcyclohexan-1-ol. When it undergoes hydroboration–oxidation, the product is 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol.
Statement II: In hydroboration, the boron atom bonds to the sp$^2$ carbon carrying fewer hydrogen atoms, because that carbon forms the more stable carbocation.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. With H$^+$/H$_2$O, a 3° carbocation forms at the methyl-bearing carbon (C-1), giving the Markovnikov product 1-methylcyclohexan-1-ol.
In hydroboration, boron goes to the ring carbon bearing H (C-2). Oxidation then places –OH there, giving 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol, the anti-Markovnikov-looking product.
Statement II is incorrect. Boron attaches to the sp$^2$ carbon carrying the greater number of hydrogen atoms, not fewer.
Hydroboration also does not proceed through a free carbocation in the way acid hydration does.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the structures of methanol, phenol and methoxymethane is INCORRECT?
options: The C–O–H bond angle in methanol is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle because of repulsion between the lone pairs on oxygen.
The C–O bond in phenol (136 pm) is shorter than in methanol, partly because oxygen is attached to an $sp^2$ hybridised carbon.
The C–O–C bond angle in methoxymethane is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle because of repulsion between the two bulky alkyl groups.
The C–O bond length in methoxymethane (141 pm) is much greater than the C–O bond length in methanol.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: repulsion between the unshared pairs on oxygen makes the angle slightly less than 109°28′.
(2) Correct: the C–O bond in phenol is shortened by partial double bond character (conjugation) and by the $sp^2$ carbon.
(3) Correct: the two bulky R groups repel each other, so the angle is slightly greater than tetrahedral.
(4) Incorrect: NCERT states that the C–O bond length in ethers (141 pm) is almost the same as in alcohols.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly compares the C–O–C or C–O–H bond angle in methoxymethane and methanol with the tetrahedral angle ($109^\circ 28'$)?
questions.explanation:
Methanol: the two lone pairs on oxygen repel the bond pairs. This makes the C–O–H angle slightly less than $109^\circ 28'$.
Methoxymethane: the two bulky methyl groups repel each other. This makes the C–O–C angle slightly greater than tetrahedral.
So the order is ether > tetrahedral > alcohol.
Option (1) reverses the roles of the two effects.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Both ethanol and phenol liberate hydrogen with sodium metal. Which reagent forms a salt with phenol but not with ethanol, and so shows that phenol is the stronger acid?
questions.explanation:
Active metals such as Na, K and Al react with both alcohols and phenols. They give alkoxides or phenoxides and $H_2$.
Phenol also reacts with aqueous NaOH to give sodium phenoxide and water. Ethanol does not do this.
So the reaction with aqueous NaOH shows that phenol is a stronger acid than both ethanol and water.
The metal options are wrong because they do not tell the two compounds apart.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: n-Pentane (b.p. 309.1 K) and ethoxyethane (b.p. 307.6 K) have nearly the same boiling point.
Statement II: Ethoxyethane boils at a higher temperature than butan-1-ol because its polar C–O bonds give it a net dipole moment.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The weak polarity of ethers does not appreciably affect their boiling points, so they resemble alkanes of comparable mass.
Statement II is incorrect. Butan-1-ol boils at 390 K, far above ethoxyethane at 307.6 K.
The reason is intermolecular hydrogen bonding in the alcohol, which ether molecules cannot form among themselves.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: tert-Butyl ethyl ether is suitably prepared by Williamson synthesis using sodium tert-butoxide and bromoethane, not sodium ethoxide and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
Statement II: Alkoxide ions are strong bases as well as nucleophiles, so with tertiary alkyl halides elimination gives an alkene instead of an ether.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement II is correct. Alkoxides act both as nucleophiles and as bases. With a tertiary halide, elimination wins; for example, sodium ethoxide with tert-butyl bromide gives 2-methylpropene.
Statement I is correct. Williamson synthesis works best when the alkoxide attacks a primary alkyl halide by SN2. So the bulky part should come from the alkoxide, $(CH_3)_3CO^-Na^+$, and the primary part from the halide, $C_2H_5Br$.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2-Methylpropene is converted to alcohol X by acid-catalysed hydration and to alcohol Y by hydroboration–oxidation. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: X gives turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent, while Y gives no turbidity at room temperature
Vapours of Y passed over heated copper at 573 K give an alkene
X is oxidised by $CrO_3$ to a ketone with the same number of carbon atoms
X and Y can be obtained from $CH_3MgBr$ by reaction with propanone and ethanal respectively, followed by hydrolysis
questions.explanation:
Identify X and Y. Acid hydration follows Markovnikov's rule, so X = 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tertiary). Hydroboration–oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov product, so Y = 2-methylpropan-1-ol (primary).
(1) Correct: a tertiary alcohol gives instant turbidity with Lucas reagent; a primary alcohol gives none at room temperature.
(2) Wrong: a primary alcohol over Cu at 573 K gives an aldehyde. Only tertiary alcohols dehydrate there.
(3) Wrong: tertiary alcohols resist oxidation.
(4) Wrong: ethanal with $CH_3MgBr$ gives propan-2-ol, not Y.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When 3-methylbutan-2-ol is treated with HBr, the major product is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, not 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.
Reason (R): The secondary carbocation formed after loss of water from the protonated alcohol rearranges into a more stable tertiary carbocation, by shift of a hydride ion from C-3.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: HBr protonates the –OH group, which then leaves as water. This gives a secondary carbocation at C-2.
Step 2: A hydride ion (H$^-$) moves from C-3 to C-2. This produces a tertiary carbocation at C-3, which is more stable.
Step 3: Br$^-$ attacks this tertiary carbon. The product is (CH$_3$)$_2$CBr–CH$_2$CH$_3$, that is, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.
So A is true, and R correctly explains it.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aspirin, a drug with analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic properties, is obtained by which reaction?
questions.explanation:
Acetylation means introducing an acetyl ($CH_3CO$) group into an alcohol or phenol.
According to NCERT, acetylation of the phenolic –OH of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) gives aspirin, i.e. acetylsalicylic acid.
Kolbe's reaction only produces salicylic acid, the starting material.
Acetylating phenol itself gives phenyl acetate, not aspirin.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol (molar mass 46) boils at a much higher temperature than propane (molar mass 44), even though their molecular masses are comparable. What is the main reason for this difference?
options: Ethanol has a larger surface area, so van der Waals forces are stronger
Ethanol molecules are linked by intermolecular hydrogen bonds
The C–O bond in ethanol is shorter than the C–C bond in propane
questions.explanation:
The –OH group of one ethanol molecule forms a hydrogen bond with the oxygen of a neighbouring molecule.
Extra energy is needed to break these intermolecular hydrogen bonds before boiling, so the boiling point is high.
Propane has only weak van der Waals forces, and its surface area is not larger than ethanol's.
Intramolecular hydrogen bonding would not raise the boiling point. It is not present in ethanol anyway.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Four isomeric alcohols of formula $C_4H_{10}O$ are separately shaken with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous $ZnCl_2$) at room temperature. Which one gives turbidity immediately?
questions.explanation:
The alcohols dissolve in Lucas reagent, but the alkyl chlorides formed are immiscible and cause turbidity.
Tertiary alcohols form halides most easily via a stable carbocation, so turbidity appears at once.
2-Methylpropan-2-ol is the only tertiary alcohol here.
Butan-2-ol is secondary and reacts more slowly.
Butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol are primary and give no turbidity at room temperature.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pKa of phenol is 10.0 and that of ethanol is 15.9. Approximately how many times greater is the acid dissociation constant ($K_a$) of phenol than that of ethanol? (Take $10^{0.9} \approx 7.94$.)
questions.explanation:
Given: pKa(phenol) = 10.0 and pKa(ethanol) = 15.9.
Formula: $K_a = 10^{-pK_a}$, so $\frac{K_a(\text{phenol})}{K_a(\text{ethanol})} = 10^{15.9-10.0}$.
Substituting: $10^{5.9} = 10^{0.9} \times 10^{5} = 7.94 \times 10^{5}$.
So phenol is roughly a million times more acidic, about $7.9 \times 10^{5}$ times.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the acid–base behaviour of alcohols is INCORRECT?
options: Alcohols react with aluminium to form the corresponding alkoxide and hydrogen gas.
Alcohols can act as Brönsted bases because of the unshared electron pairs on oxygen.
Sodium ethoxide is a weaker base than sodium hydroxide.
Alcohols are Brönsted acids because they can donate a proton to a stronger base.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Na, K and Al react with alcohols to give alkoxides and $H_2$.
(2) Correct: the lone pairs on oxygen let an alcohol accept a proton.
(3) Incorrect: alcohols are weaker acids than water. So the alkoxide ion is a better proton acceptor than $OH^-$, which makes sodium ethoxide the stronger base.
(4) Correct: this is the Brönsted acid behaviour of alcohols.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about reactions of phenol are correct?
(i) Treating phenol with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ and then with conc. HNO$_3$ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol.
(ii) In the Reimer–Tiemann reaction, a substituted benzal chloride intermediate is hydrolysed by alkali to give salicylaldehyde.
(iii) Phenol itself reacts with CO$_2$ in Kolbe's reaction more readily than the phenoxide ion does.
(iv) Chromic acid oxidises phenol to a conjugated diketone.
(v) 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol is a strong acid because its three –NO$_2$ groups withdraw electrons and help release H$^+$.
(vi) Phenol exposed to air is slowly oxidised to pure, colourless benzoquinone.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is the modern route to picric acid, via phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid.
(ii) Correct: the benzal chloride intermediate is hydrolysed in alkali to salicylaldehyde.
(iii) Incorrect: the phenoxide ion is more reactive than phenol, which is why Kolbe's reaction uses NaOH.
(iv) Correct: the product is benzoquinone, a conjugated diketone.
(v) Correct: the electron-withdrawing –NO$_2$ groups make picric acid a strong acid.
(vi) Incorrect: air oxidation gives dark-coloured mixtures containing quinones, not pure colourless benzoquinone.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 2-Methylpropan-2-ol undergoes acid-catalysed dehydration under milder conditions than ethanol.
Reason (R): In acid-catalysed dehydration, formation of the carbocation from the protonated alcohol is the slowest step, and a tertiary carbocation is more stable than a primary one.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Ethanol needs conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 443 K, while tertiary alcohols dehydrate under milder conditions. The order of ease is 3° > 2° > 1°.
R is true. Step 2, formation of the carbocation, is rate-determining. The tertiary carbocation is the most stable and forms most easily.
The easier rate-determining step is exactly what makes tertiary dehydration easier, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a simple (symmetrical) ether?
questions.explanation:
An ether is symmetrical (simple) when both groups on the oxygen are the same. It is unsymmetrical (mixed) when the two groups differ.
(a) Ethyl and methyl groups: mixed ether.
(b) Ethyl and phenyl groups (phenetole): mixed ether.
(c) Two ethyl groups (diethyl ether): symmetrical ether.
(d) Methyl and phenyl groups (anisole): mixed ether.
Answer: (c)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $C_6H_5-O-(CH_2)_6-CH_3$ is named 1-phenoxyheptane, whereas $C_6H_5-O-CH_3$ is named methoxybenzene.
Reason (R): In the IUPAC naming of ethers, the larger group is chosen as the parent hydrocarbon and the other group is written as the alkoxy/aryloxy substituent.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Heptyl (7 C) is larger than phenyl (6 C), so heptane is the parent and $C_6H_5O-$ is the phenoxy substituent at C-1. In anisole, phenyl (6 C) is larger than methyl (1 C), so benzene is the parent.
R is true and is exactly the NCERT rule for naming ethers.
R therefore explains both names given in A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about electrophilic substitution in phenol are correct?
(i) Phenol with dilute HNO$_3$ at 298 K gives a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol.
(ii) p-Nitrophenol is more volatile than o-nitrophenol.
(iii) The –OH group directs electrophiles to the ortho and para positions because resonance makes these positions electron rich.
(iv) Bromination of phenol takes place only in the presence of a Lewis acid such as FeBr$_3$.
(v) Concentrated HNO$_3$ converts phenol to 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, but the yield is poor.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: dilute HNO$_3$ at low temperature gives the o/p mixture.
(ii) Incorrect: the ortho isomer is the more volatile one, because of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
(iii) Correct: the resonance effect of –OH increases electron density at the o and p positions.
(iv) Incorrect: the –OH group itself polarises Br$_2$, so no Lewis acid is needed.
(v) Correct: this is direct nitration to picric acid, which gives a poor yield.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following statements.
Statement I: The C–O bond length in phenol (136 pm) is slightly shorter than the C–O bond length in methanol.
Statement II: The C–O–C bond angle in ethers is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle because of repulsion between the two bulky alkyl groups.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The C–O bond in phenol is shorter for two reasons. The lone pair on oxygen conjugates with the ring, which gives the bond partial double bond character. The carbon attached to oxygen is also $sp^2$ hybridised.
