Statement II is correct. In ethers, the two bulky R groups repel each other, so the C–O–C angle opens slightly beyond $109^\circ 28'$.
Both statements are correct.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent with substrate) with List-II (type of product).
List-I:
(A) PCC with a primary alcohol
(B) Acidified $KMnO_4$ with a primary alcohol
(C) $CrO_3$ with a secondary alcohol
(D) $PBr_3$ with a primary alcohol
List-II:
(I) Ketone
(II) Alkyl bromide
(III) Aldehyde
(IV) Carboxylic acid
questions.explanation:
(A) PCC is a mild reagent and stops at the aldehyde, so A matches III.
(B) Strong oxidants like acidified $KMnO_4$ take a primary alcohol directly to the carboxylic acid, so B matches IV.
(C) $CrO_3$ oxidises a secondary alcohol to a ketone, so C matches I.
(D) $PBr_3$ converts an alcohol into an alkyl bromide, so D matches II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the present-day commercial manufacture of methanol, carbon monoxide is hydrogenated at high pressure and temperature in the presence of which catalyst?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: most methanol is now made by catalytic hydrogenation of CO at high pressure and temperature.
The catalyst used is a mixture of zinc oxide and chromium(III) oxide, ZnO–Cr$_2$O$_3$.
Nickel is the tempting wrong option because it is used to hydrogenate C=C and C=O bonds. It is not the catalyst for CO + H$_2$ → CH$_3$OH.
V$_2$O$_5$ belongs to the contact process, and AlCl$_3$ is a Friedel–Crafts catalyst.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the manufacture of phenol from cumene are correct?
(i) Cumene is isopropylbenzene.
(ii) Cumene is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide.
(iii) Cumene hydroperoxide gives phenol and acetone when treated with dilute acid.
(iv) Acetone is obtained in large quantities as a by-product of this process.
(v) Cumene hydroperoxide is converted to phenol by fusion with molten NaOH at 623 K.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: cumene is isopropylbenzene.
(ii) Correct: it is oxidised in the presence of air to cumene hydroperoxide.
(iii) Correct: dilute acid splits the hydroperoxide into phenol and acetone.
(iv) Correct: large quantities of acetone are obtained this way.
(v) Incorrect: the conversion uses dilute acid, not molten NaOH.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the modern preparation of picric acid, phenol is first treated with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ to give X, and X is then treated with concentrated HNO$_3$ to give Y. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: X is phenol-3,5-disulphonic acid, and Y is 3,5-dinitrophenol
X is phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid, and Y is a weak acid, less acidic than phenol
X is phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid, and Y is a strong acid because its three –NO$_2$ groups favour release of H$^+$
X is 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, and Y is its sulphonic acid derivative
questions.explanation:
Direct nitration of phenol with concentrated HNO$_3$ gives picric acid in poor yield, so phenol is sulphonated first.
Concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ gives phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid (X). Substitution is ortho/para, so the 3,5-isomer is ruled out.
Concentrated HNO$_3$ then converts X to 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (Y), which is picric acid.
The three electron-withdrawing –NO$_2$ groups stabilise the phenoxide ion, so picric acid is a strong acid, far stronger than phenol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: m-Nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol but less acidic than p-nitrophenol.
Statement II: A –NO2 group at the meta position delocalises the negative charge of the phenoxide ion onto its own oxygen atoms by resonance, just as it does from the para position.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The pKa values are p-nitrophenol 7.1 < m-nitrophenol 8.3 < phenol 10.0, and a lower pKa means a stronger acid.
Statement II is incorrect. In the phenoxide ion, the negative charge reaches only the ortho and para positions.
A meta –NO2 group therefore cannot take the charge by resonance. It raises acidity only through its electron-withdrawing inductive effect.
That is why the effect is weaker at meta than at ortho or para.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pKa of p-nitrophenol is 7.1 and that of phenol is 10.0. Approximately how many times greater is the acid dissociation constant ($K_a$) of p-nitrophenol than that of phenol? (Take $10^{0.9} \approx 7.94$)
questions.explanation:
Given: pKa (p-nitrophenol) = 7.1 and pKa (phenol) = 10.0.
Formula: $K_a = 10^{-pK_a}$, so the ratio is $\frac{K_{a1}}{K_{a2}} = 10^{(pK_{a2}-pK_{a1})}$.
Substituting: ratio = $10^{(10.0-7.1)} = 10^{2.9} = 10^{0.9} \times 10^2 \approx 7.94 \times 100$.
So the $K_a$ of p-nitrophenol is about 794 times that of phenol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Propene is first treated with diborane, $(BH_3)_2$, and the product is then oxidised with $H_2O_2$ in aqueous NaOH. The alcohol obtained is:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: in hydroboration, boron attaches to the sp$^2$ carbon that carries more hydrogen atoms. For propene, this is the terminal CH$_2$.
Oxidation with $H_2O_2$/NaOH replaces boron by –OH, giving CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH (propan-1-ol).
The result looks like water added against Markovnikov's rule.
Propan-2-ol would come from acid-catalysed hydration instead.
A diol is not formed, because only one –OH is introduced per double bond.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider all the structurally isomeric alcohols with molecular formula $C_5H_{12}O$ (ignore stereoisomers). The numbers of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols among them are, respectively:
questions.explanation:
Primary (4): pentan-1-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol, 3-methylbutan-1-ol and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol.
Secondary (3): pentan-2-ol, pentan-3-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
Tertiary (1): 2-methylbutan-2-ol.
This gives 8 structural isomers in total, split as 4, 3, 1.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane, $(CH_3)_3C–O–CH_3$, on heating with HI gives 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol.
Reason (R): In the cleavage of ethers by HI, iodide ion always attacks the less hindered methyl carbon of the oxonium ion by an $S_N2$ mechanism.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the products are tert-butyl iodide and CH3OH.
R is false: the word 'always' is wrong. When one group is tertiary, CH3OH leaves the protonated ether to form the stable $(CH_3)_3C^+$ carbocation.
$I^-$ then attacks this carbocation, so the reaction follows $S_N1$.
If R were true, the products would be CH3I and tert-butyl alcohol, which contradicts A.
$S_N2$ attack at the less substituted carbon applies only when primary or secondary groups are present.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (pKa value):
List-I
(A) p-Nitrophenol
(B) m-Nitrophenol
(C) m-Cresol
(D) Ethanol
List-II
(I) 15.9
(II) 10.1
(III) 8.3
(IV) 7.1
questions.explanation:
A: p-Nitrophenol is the strongest acid in the list, because –$NO_2$ at the para position delocalises the charge. Its pKa is 7.1 (IV).
B: m-Nitrophenol is weaker than the para isomer but stronger than phenol. Its pKa is 8.3 (III).
C: m-Cresol is slightly weaker than phenol because –$CH_3$ releases electrons. Its pKa is 10.1 (II).
D: Ethanol is the weakest acid here, with a pKa of 15.9 (I).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pKa of p-nitrophenol is 7.1 and that of phenol is 10.0. By approximately what factor is the acid dissociation constant $K_a$ of p-nitrophenol greater than that of phenol? (antilog 0.9 = 7.94)
questions.explanation:
Given: pKa of p-nitrophenol = 7.1 and pKa of phenol = 10.0.
Formula: $K_a = 10^{-pK_a}$, so the ratio of the two $K_a$ values is $10^{\Delta pK_a}$.
Substituting: $\Delta pK_a = 10.0 - 7.1 = 2.9$, so the ratio is $10^{2.9} = 7.94 \times 10^2$.
So $K_a$ of p-nitrophenol is about 794 times that of phenol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol, $(CH_3)_3C-CH(OH)-CH_3$, is heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$. What is the major alkene formed?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Protonation of –OH and loss of water give a 2° carbocation at C-2. This is the slow step.
Step 2: A methyl group shifts from C-3 to C-2. This converts the cation into the more stable 3° carbocation $(CH_3)_2C^+-CH(CH_3)_2$.
Step 3: A proton is lost from the adjacent CH. This gives the more substituted (tetrasubstituted) alkene, $(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$, which is 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene would form only if no rearrangement occurred, so it is a minor product.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Alcohols are converted to alkyl bromides by phosphorus tribromide.
Thionyl chloride converts alcohols to alkyl chlorides, and both by-products ($SO_2$ and HCl) escape as gases.
In the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol, the formation of the carbocation is the slowest, rate-determining step.
In the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol, the acid used to protonate the alcohol is consumed and is not regenerated.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $PBr_3$ converts alcohols to alkyl bromides.
(2) Correct: $ROH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow RCl + SO_2 + HCl$. The gaseous by-products escape, leaving the halide fairly pure.
(3) Correct: NCERT names carbocation formation (step 2) as the slowest, rate-determining step.
(4) Incorrect: the proton used in step 1 is released again in step 3 when the alkene forms. The acid therefore acts as a catalyst.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the production of ethanol from molasses, the sugar is first converted into glucose and fructose. Which enzyme brings about this conversion?
questions.explanation:
The sugar in molasses, sugarcane or grapes is hydrolysed to glucose and fructose. Both have the formula C$_6$H$_{12}$O$_6$.
The enzyme for this step is invertase.
Zymase, found in yeast, acts in the next step: it ferments glucose and fructose to ethanol and CO$_2$. That is why zymase is the tempting distractor.
Diastase and maltase act on starch and maltose, not on cane sugar.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the preparation of phenol is INCORRECT?
options: When benzene diazonium chloride is warmed with water, nitrogen gas is liberated along with the formation of phenol.
Benzene can be converted to phenol using only oleum, NaOH and an acid for the final step.
When benzenesulphonic acid is heated with molten NaOH, free phenol is obtained directly and no acidification is required.
Converting chlorobenzene to phenol with NaOH needs a high temperature (623 K) and a high pressure (320 atm).
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the diazonium salt is hydrolysed to phenol, and $N_2$ and HCl are released.
(2) Correct: oleum sulphonates benzene, molten NaOH gives sodium phenoxide, and acid then frees phenol.
(3) Incorrect: molten NaOH gives sodium phenoxide, and acidification is required to obtain phenol.
(4) Correct: these drastic conditions are needed for the haloarene route.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (structural feature) with List-II (reason).
List-I
(A) C–O–H angle in methanol slightly below 109°28′
(B) C–O bond in phenol (136 pm) shorter than in methanol
(C) C–O–C angle in methoxymethane slightly above 109°28′
(D) C–O bond length in ethers (141 pm) almost the same as in alcohols
List-II
(i) Repulsion between two bulky alkyl groups
(ii) Repulsion between unshared electron pairs on oxygen
(iii) Conjugation of oxygen lone pair with the ring and sp$^2$ carbon
(iv) In both, an sp$^3$ carbon is bonded to an sp$^3$ oxygen
questions.explanation:
(A) In alcohols, lone pair–lone pair repulsion compresses the C–O–H angle, so A matches (ii).
(B) In phenol, conjugation gives the C–O bond partial double bond character, and the carbon is sp$^2$. Both shorten the bond, so B matches (iii).
(C) In ethers, the bulky R groups repel each other and widen the angle, so C matches (i).
(D) Both ethers and alcohols have a C$_{sp^3}$–O$_{sp^3}$ sigma bond, so their lengths are similar. D matches (iv).
Answer: (a)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Esterification of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid is carried out with a small amount of conc. $H_2SO_4$.
(ii) Esterification with a carboxylic acid is reversible, so water is removed as soon as it is formed.
(iii) Acetylation of salicylic acid produces aspirin.
(iv) Aspirin has analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic properties.
(v) Phenols cannot be acetylated because their O–H bond does not break.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a small amount of conc. $H_2SO_4$ is used as the catalyst.
(ii) Correct: the reaction is reversible, so water is removed to push it forward.
(iii) Correct: aspirin is formed by acetylation of salicylic acid.
(iv) Correct: NCERT lists all three properties for aspirin.
(v) Incorrect: phenols also form esters through O–H cleavage. Salicylic acid itself is acetylated at its phenolic –OH.
So four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: A benzene diazonium salt is prepared by treating aniline with nitrous acid ($NaNO_2$ + HCl) at 273–278 K.
Statement II: Benzene diazonium chloride gives phenol when warmed with water or treated with dilute acid.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. An aromatic primary amine such as aniline reacts with $NaNO_2$ + HCl at 273–278 K to form the diazonium salt.
Statement II is correct. Warming the diazonium salt with water, or treating it with dilute acid, hydrolyses it to phenol. $N_2$ and HCl are released.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Acid-catalysed hydration of propene gives propan-2-ol as the major product.
Reason (R): In the first step, $H_3O^+$ protonates propene to form the more stable secondary carbocation, which is then attacked by a water molecule.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Hydration of an unsymmetrical alkene follows Markovnikov's rule, so OH ends up on C-2.
R is true. The mechanism has three steps:
(1) protonation of the alkene by $H_3O^+$ to give a carbocation;
(2) nucleophilic attack of $H_2O$ on the carbocation;
(3) deprotonation to give the alcohol.
The proton adds to $CH_2$, giving the 2° carbocation $CH_3\overset{+}{C}HCH_3$. This places OH on C-2, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given pKa values: phenol 10.0, o-nitrophenol 7.2, m-nitrophenol 8.3, p-nitrophenol 7.1, o-cresol 10.2, m-cresol 10.1, p-cresol 10.2, ethanol 15.9.
How many of the compounds listed (other than phenol) are stronger acids than phenol?
questions.explanation:
A lower pKa means a stronger acid, so we need pKa < 10.0.
o-Nitrophenol (7.2), m-nitrophenol (8.3) and p-nitrophenol (7.1) qualify. The electron-withdrawing –$NO_2$ group stabilises the phenoxide ion.
All three cresols (10.1–10.2) are weaker acids, because electron-releasing –$CH_3$ destabilises phenoxide.
Ethanol (15.9) is far weaker.
Count = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Phenoxide ion is more stable than phenol because the resonance structures of phenol involve charge separation.
(ii) In an alkoxide ion, the negative charge is delocalised over the alkyl group.
(iii) The sp² carbon bearing –OH in phenol lowers the electron density on oxygen and increases the polarity of the O–H bond.
(iv) Picric acid is a strong acid because of its three electron-withdrawing –NO2 groups.
(v) Cresols are more acidic than phenol because the methyl group stabilises the phenoxide ion.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: phenoxide ion delocalises its charge without charge separation, so it is more stable than phenol.
(ii) Incorrect: the charge in an alkoxide ion is localised on oxygen.
(iii) Correct: the sp² carbon is more electronegative than an sp³ carbon, so the O–H bond is more polar.
(iv) Correct: the three –NO2 groups help release H⁺.
(v) Incorrect: –CH3 is electron-releasing and destabilises phenoxide, so cresols are less acidic (pKa about 10.1–10.2).
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The cleavage of the C–O bond in ethers is brought about by hydrogen halides. What is the correct order of reactivity of hydrogen halides in this reaction?
questions.explanation:
Ethers are the least reactive of these functional groups. Their C–O bond breaks only under drastic conditions with excess hydrogen halide.
The reaction begins with protonation of the ether, so the acid must be strong. Its halide ion must then act as a good nucleophile.
HI is the strongest acid, and I$^-$ is the best nucleophile among the halide ions. HBr comes next, and HCl is the least effective.
So the order is HI > HBr > HCl. Concentrated HI or HBr at high temperature is used in practice.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Propene is treated with water in the presence of dilute sulphuric acid. What is the major product?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: acid-catalysed hydration of an unsymmetrical alkene follows Markovnikov's rule.
H$^+$ adds to the terminal CH$_2$ carbon, which carries more hydrogen atoms. This forms the more stable secondary carbocation CH$_3$–CH$^+$–CH$_3$.
Water attacks this carbocation, and loss of a proton then gives CH$_3$CH(OH)CH$_3$, which is propan-2-ol.
Propan-1-ol is the anti-Markovnikov product. It comes from hydroboration–oxidation, not from acid hydration.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2-Ethoxy-3-methylpentane, $CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)OC_2H_5$, is to be made by Williamson synthesis using ethanol and 3-methylpentan-2-ol as the organic starting materials. Which sequence gives the ether in the best yield?
options: Convert 3-methylpentan-2-ol to 2-bromo-3-methylpentane with HBr, then treat it with sodium ethoxide
Convert ethanol to bromoethane with HBr, then treat it with sodium 3-methylpentan-2-oxide (made using Na)
Heat ethanol and 3-methylpentan-2-ol together with conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 443 K
Convert both alcohols to their sodium alkoxides and mix them
questions.explanation:
The alkyl halide should be primary so that SN2 dominates over elimination.
In option (2), bromoethane is primary and the secondary alkoxide acts as the nucleophile, so substitution gives the ether (this is the NCERT route).
Option (1) uses a secondary halide with a strongly basic ethoxide, so elimination competes and yields alkenes.
Option (3) happens at a temperature that favours alkenes, and a mixed alcohol system gives a mixture.
Option (4) has no leaving group, so no reaction occurs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fermentation of grape juice for wine making must be carried out in the absence of air.
Reason (R): Oxygen of air oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid, which spoils the taste of alcoholic drinks.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT says fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions, i.e. in the absence of air.
R is true: if air enters the mixture, its oxygen oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid. This destroys the taste of the drink.
R explains why air must be kept out, so it is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the reaction of phenol in List-I with the main product in List-II.
List-I
(A) $CHCl_3$ + aq. NaOH, then hydrolysis
(B) NaOH, then $CO_2$, then $H^+$
(C) Heating with zinc dust
(D) Chromic acid
List-II
(P) Benzoquinone
(Q) Benzene
(R) Salicylaldehyde
(S) ortho-Hydroxybenzoic acid
questions.explanation:
(A) Reimer–Tiemann reaction introduces –CHO at the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde (R).
(B) Kolbe's reaction gives ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (S).
(C) Zinc dust removes the –OH group, giving benzene (Q).
(D) Chromic acid oxidises phenol to the conjugated diketone benzoquinone (P).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of $HOCH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_3$ is:
questions.explanation:
The longest chain containing both –OH carbons has 5 C, so the parent is pentane.
Numbering from the $CH_2OH$ end puts the –OH groups at 1 and 4; numbering from the other end gives 2 and 5. Lower locants win, so the –OH groups are at 1 and 4 and the methyl is at C-2.
For a diol, the 'e' of the alkane is retained: pentane-1,4-diol.
So the name is 2-methylpentane-1,4-diol. Option (2) wrongly drops the 'e', and option (1) uses higher locants.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: A patient poisoned by methanol is treated with intravenous infusions of diluted ethanol.
Statement II: Ethanol reacts with methanol in the body to form a non-toxic ether, which is then excreted by the kidneys.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: NCERT describes treating methanol poisoning with diluted ethanol given intravenously.
Statement II is incorrect: no ether is formed in the body.
Methanol is oxidised in the body to methanal and then to methanoic acid, which can cause blindness and death.
The added ethanol swamps the enzyme that oxidises the aldehyde to the acid. This slows the toxic oxidation and gives the kidneys time to excrete the methanol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Which of the following correctly arranges the compounds in INCREASING order of acid strength?
(P) $(CH_3)_3COH$ (Q) $CH_3CH_2OH$ (R) $H_2O$ (S) p-cresol (T) phenol (U) 2,4,6-trinitrophenol
options: Q < P < R < S < T < U
P < Q < R < S < T < U
P < Q < R < T < S < U
R < P < Q < S < T < U
questions.explanation:
Among alcohols, acid strength follows 1° > 2° > 3°, because alkyl groups release electrons. So tert-butyl alcohol is weaker than ethanol: P < Q.
Alcohols are weaker acids than water: Q < R.
Phenols are stronger acids than water. The –$CH_3$ group in p-cresol (pKa 10.2) makes it weaker than phenol (pKa 10.0): R < S < T.
Picric acid has three –$NO_2$ groups and is a strong acid: T < U.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is shaken with an aqueous solution of bromine (bromine water) at room temperature. What is the observed product?
options: A mixture of o- and p-bromophenol remaining in solution
questions.explanation:
Bromine water is a polar medium, and the –OH group strongly activates the ring.
All the ortho and para positions (2, 4 and 6) are therefore brominated.
The product, 2,4,6-tribromophenol, separates as a white precipitate.
Monobromophenols form only in solvents of low polarity such as CS$_2$ or CHCl$_3$ at low temperature, so option (1) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Heating 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane with HI gives methanol and 2-iodo-2-methylpropane.
Reason (R): In the cleavage of every ether by HI, the iodide ion attacks the least substituted carbon of the protonated ether by an $S_N2$ mechanism.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. The ether contains a tertiary alkyl group, and NCERT shows that HI cleaves it to methanol and tert-butyl iodide.
R is false. When one group is tertiary, the protonated ether loses CH$_3$OH to form the stable carbocation (CH$_3$)$_3$C$^+$. Iodide then attacks this carbocation, so the reaction follows an $S_N1$ mechanism.
The $S_N2$ attack at the less substituted carbon applies only when primary or secondary groups are present. If it applied here, the products would be methyl iodide and tert-butyl alcohol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenetole, $C_6H_5OCH_2CH_3$, is an alkyl aryl ether. What is its IUPAC name?
questions.explanation:
In IUPAC naming, an ether is treated as a hydrocarbon in which one H is replaced by an –OR or –OAr group.
The larger group becomes the parent hydrocarbon. The phenyl ring ($C_6$) is larger than ethyl ($C_2$), so benzene is the parent and $–OC_2H_5$ is the ethoxy substituent. The name is ethoxybenzene.
Phenoxyethane wrongly makes the smaller ethyl group the parent.
Ethyl phenyl ether is the common name.
Methoxybenzene is anisole.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm, the product obtained before any acid is added is sodium phenoxide, not phenol.
Reason (R): Phenol is acidic and reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium phenoxide.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The fusion gives sodium phenoxide, and phenol is set free only when the mixture is acidified.
R is true. Phenol is acidic enough to react with aqueous NaOH and form sodium phenoxide.
In the reaction mixture, excess NaOH converts any phenol formed into its salt. R therefore explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following alcohols are NOT oxidised by $CrO_3$ under normal conditions?
2-Methylpropan-2-ol, butan-2-ol, propan-1-ol, 1-methylcyclohexanol, cyclohexanol, 2-methylbutan-2-ol, phenylmethanol, 3-methylpentan-3-ol
questions.explanation:
Tertiary alcohols have no H atom on the carbinol carbon, so they resist oxidation under normal conditions.
The tertiary alcohols in the list are 2-methylpropan-2-ol, 1-methylcyclohexanol, 2-methylbutan-2-ol and 3-methylpentan-3-ol, which makes 4.
Butan-2-ol and cyclohexanol are 2° alcohols and are oxidised to ketones.
Propan-1-ol and phenylmethanol are 1° alcohols and are oxidised to aldehydes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanoic acid is treated with lithium aluminium hydride, followed by water. The product is:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: LiAlH$_4$ is a strong reducing agent. It reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols in excellent yield: RCOOH $\rightarrow$ RCH$_2$OH.
Here R = CH$_3$, so CH$_3$COOH gives CH$_3$CH$_2$OH (ethanol).
The carbon count stays the same, so methanol is wrong.
The reduction does not stop at the aldehyde (ethanal) stage under these conditions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid gives a conjugated diketone. What is this compound?
questions.explanation:
Chromic acid oxidises phenol to benzoquinone, which is a conjugated cyclic diketone.
In air, phenols are slowly oxidised to dark-coloured mixtures containing quinones.
Hydroquinone (benzene-1,4-diol) and catechol (benzene-1,2-diol) are diols, not diketones.
Salicylaldehyde is an aldehyde formed in the Reimer–Tiemann reaction.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alcohols produces turbidity immediately at room temperature when shaken with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous $ZnCl_2$)?
questions.explanation:
Lucas reagent dissolves alcohols, but the alkyl chlorides formed are immiscible, so they appear as turbidity.
Tertiary alcohols form the halide fastest, through a stable 3° carbocation, so the turbidity is immediate.
2-Methylpropan-2-ol, $(CH_3)_3COH$, is the only tertiary alcohol among the options.
Butan-2-ol (2°) reacts more slowly. Butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol (both 1°) give no turbidity at room temperature.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the starting material in List-I with the sequence of reagents and conditions in List-II that converts it into phenol.
List-I
(a) Chlorobenzene
(b) Benzene
(c) Aniline
(d) Cumene
List-II
(i) $NaNO_2$ + HCl at 273–278 K, then warming with water
(ii) Air (O$_2$), then dilute acid
(iii) NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm, then acidification
(iv) Oleum, then fusion with molten NaOH, then acidification
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm. This gives sodium phenoxide, and acidifying it gives phenol: (iii).
(b) Benzene is first sulphonated with oleum to benzenesulphonic acid. Fusing this with molten NaOH and then acidifying gives phenol: (iv).
(c) Aniline is diazotised with $NaNO_2$/HCl at 273–278 K. Warming the diazonium salt with water gives phenol: (i).
(d) Cumene is air-oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide. Dilute acid then splits it into phenol and acetone: (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Phenol undergoes bromination even without a Lewis acid such as FeBr$_3$, whereas benzene needs one.
Statement II: Heating phenol directly with concentrated nitric acid is the preferred method because it gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol in excellent yield.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The –OH group activates the ring so strongly that the bromine molecule gets polarised even without a Lewis acid.
Statement II is incorrect. Direct nitration with concentrated HNO$_3$ does give picric acid, but the yield is poor.
Picric acid is now made by first sulphonating phenol with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ to phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid, then nitrating with concentrated HNO$_3$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction) with List-II (main organic product):
List-I
(A) $C_2H_5OH$ + conc. $H_2SO_4$, 443 K
(B) $C_2H_5OH$ + conc. $H_2SO_4$, 413 K
(C) $C_6H_5ONa$ + $CH_3Br$
(D) $CH_3ONa$ + $(CH_3)_3CBr$
List-II
(I) Methoxybenzene
(II) 2-Methylpropene
(III) Ethene
(IV) Ethoxyethane
questions.explanation:
(A) At 443 K, ethanol undergoes intramolecular dehydration to give ethene (III).
(B) At the lower temperature of 413 K, ethoxyethane (IV) is the main product.
(C) Phenoxide attacks the primary halide CH₃Br by SN2 in Williamson synthesis, giving methoxybenzene, or anisole (I).
(D) With a tertiary halide, methoxide acts as a base and gives only 2-methylpropene (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol is steam distilled, o-nitrophenol distils over and p-nitrophenol stays behind.
Reason (R): p-Nitrophenol shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which holds its molecules together.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile because its –OH and –NO$_2$ groups form an intramolecular hydrogen bond, so its molecules do not associate.
R is false. p-Nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which associate its molecules and lower its volatility.
An intramolecular hydrogen bond lies within one molecule and cannot hold separate molecules together.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ethoxyethane (b.p. 307.6 K) boils at a much lower temperature than butan-1-ol (b.p. 390 K), although both have comparable molecular masses.
Reason (R): The C–O bonds in ethers are non-polar, so ether molecules have zero dipole moment.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Butan-1-ol molecules are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Ether molecules cannot form such bonds with each other, so ethoxyethane boils much lower.
R is false. The C–O bonds in ethers are polar, and ethers have a net dipole moment. This weak polarity simply does not raise their boiling points much.
The real reason for A is hydrogen bonding in the alcohol, not a lack of polarity in the ether.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are weaker acids than phenol?
o-Cresol, m-cresol, p-cresol, ethanol, water, m-nitrophenol, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol
questions.explanation:
Cresols: the electron-releasing –$CH_3$ group lowers acidity. Their pKa values (10.1–10.2) are above phenol's 10.0, so all three count.
Ethanol (pKa 15.9) is weaker, so it counts.
Water is weaker, because phenol reacts with aqueous NaOH, showing it is stronger than water. It counts.
m-Nitrophenol (pKa 8.3) is stronger than phenol.
Picric acid is stronger still, because it has three –$NO_2$ groups.
Total = 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about cleavage of ethers by concentrated HI on heating:
(i) Methoxybenzene gives phenol and iodomethane.
(ii) 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane gives 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol.
(iii) 1-Methoxypropane (with one equivalent of HI) gives iodomethane and propan-1-ol.
(iv) With excess HI, the phenol formed in (i) is converted to iodobenzene.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the O–$CH_3$ bond is weaker than O–$C_6H_5$, which has partial double bond character, so $I^-$ attacks methyl.
(ii) Correct: the stable $(CH_3)_3C^+$ forms ($S_N1$), so the tertiary iodide results.
(iii) Correct: with primary groups, $I^-$ attacks the less substituted carbon ($S_N2$), giving $CH_3I$.
(iv) Incorrect: the $sp^2$ carbon of phenol does not undergo nucleophilic substitution.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) is classified as which type of alcohol?
questions.explanation:
Alcohols are classified as mono-, di-, tri- or polyhydric according to the number of –OH groups they contain.
Glycerol, HOCH$_2$–CH(OH)–CH$_2$OH, carries three –OH groups, one on each carbon, so it is trihydric.
Ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) has two –OH groups and is the usual dihydric example, so (b) does not fit glycerol.
All three –OH groups are on sp$^3$ carbons, so glycerol is not vinylic.
Answer: (c)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will NOT give 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3$, as the major product?
options: 2-Methylbut-2-ene + H$_2$O in presence of dilute H$_2$SO$_4$
questions.explanation:
(1) CH$_3$ adds to the C=O carbon of CH$_3$COC$_2$H$_5$. The resulting 3° alcohol carries CH$_3$, CH$_3$ and C$_2$H$_5$ groups, which is 2-methylbutan-2-ol. Suitable.
(2) C$_2$H$_5$ adds to (CH$_3$)$_2$CO and gives the same 3° alcohol. Suitable.
(3) H$^+$ adds to C-3, giving a 3° carbocation at C-2. Water then attacks C-2, giving 2-methylbutan-2-ol (Markovnikov). Suitable.
(4) Boron attaches to C-3, the carbon carrying the hydrogen, so –OH ends up at C-3. The product is 3-methylbutan-2-ol, not the target. Not suitable.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (conversion) with List-II (reagent/condition used).
List-I
(A) Chlorobenzene → phenol
(B) Benzenesulphonic acid → phenol
(C) Benzene diazonium chloride → phenol
(D) Cumene hydroperoxide → phenol
List-II
(i) Warming with water
(ii) Dilute acid, acetone formed along with phenol
(iii) NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm, followed by acidification
(iv) Heating with molten NaOH, followed by acidification
questions.explanation:
(A) Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623 K and 320 atm, then acidified: (iii).
(B) Benzenesulphonic acid is heated with molten NaOH to give sodium phenoxide, which is then acidified: (iv).
(C) The diazonium salt is hydrolysed by warm water: (i).
(D) Cumene hydroperoxide with dilute acid gives phenol and acetone: (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $LiAlH_4$ reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols in excellent yield. Even so, carboxylic acids are converted to alcohols on a commercial scale by:
options: First converting them into esters, then reducing the esters by catalytic hydrogenation
questions.explanation:
NCERT: $LiAlH_4$ is a strong reducing agent but expensive, so it is used only for special chemicals.
Commercially, the acid is first esterified with an alcohol in the presence of $H^+$.
The ester is then reduced with $H_2$ over a catalyst (catalytic hydrogenation) to give the primary alcohol.
The other options are not methods described for reducing acids to alcohols.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When a small piece of sodium metal is added to dry ethanol, the products formed are:
questions.explanation:
Alcohols react with active metals (Na, K, Al) through cleavage of the O–H bond.
The products are the metal alkoxide and H2: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2.
This reaction shows that ethanol is acidic.
Water is not formed, because the hydrogen leaves as H2. Ethene arises from acid dehydration, not from reaction with Na.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following routes will NOT give 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3$, as the major product?
questions.explanation:
(1) Gives the target. Adding $C_2H_5$ to the C=O carbon of $(CH_3)_2C=O$ gives $(CH_3)_2C(OH)C_2H_5$, a 3° alcohol.
(2) Gives the target. Adding $CH_3$ to $CH_3COC_2H_5$ gives the same tertiary alcohol.
(3) Gives the target. Protonating the $=CH_2$ end forms a 3° carbocation, and water attacks there (Markovnikov).
(4) Does not. In $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$, boron attaches to the =CH carbon, which carries more H. Oxidation gives 3-methylbutan-2-ol, a 2° alcohol.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An alcohol A ($C_4H_{10}O$) does not give turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent, but turbidity appears on standing for a few minutes at room temperature. When the vapours of A are passed over heated copper at 573 K, B is formed. Heating A with conc. $H_2SO_4$ gives C as the major product. B and C are respectively
questions.explanation:
Turbidity that is delayed but appears at room temperature indicates a 2° alcohol. The only secondary $C_4H_{10}O$ alcohol is butan-2-ol, so A is butan-2-ol.
Over Cu at 573 K, a 2° alcohol is dehydrogenated to a ketone, so B is butanone.
Acid dehydration proceeds through the 2° carbocation. Loss of a proton gives mainly the more substituted alkene, so C is but-2-ene.
Both the aldehyde options correspond to primary alcohols, which give no turbidity at room temperature.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
The following four compounds are isomers with molecular formula $C_4H_{10}O$:
butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, ethoxyethane
Which option arranges them in increasing order of boiling point?
questions.explanation:
All four compounds have the same molecular mass, so the difference in boiling point comes from intermolecular forces.
Ethoxyethane has no O–H group and cannot form intermolecular H-bonds. Its boiling point is close to that of an alkane, so it is the lowest.
The three alcohols form intermolecular H-bonds. Among them, more branching means a smaller surface area and weaker van der Waals forces, which lowers the boiling point.
Branching order: 2-methylpropan-2-ol (most branched) > butan-2-ol > butan-1-ol (straight chain). This gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol < butan-2-ol < butan-1-ol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: p-Cresol is correctly named in the IUPAC system as:
questions.explanation:
Cresols are methylphenols. In phenol, the carbon carrying –OH is numbered C-1.
In the para isomer, the methyl group sits at C-4, so p-cresol is 4-methylphenol.
o-Cresol is 2-methylphenol and m-cresol is 3-methylphenol.
Option (4) is not a valid IUPAC name.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium ethoxide is a stronger base than sodium hydroxide.
Reason (R): Ethanol is a weaker proton donor than water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
In the reaction RO⁻ + H2O → ROH + OH⁻, water donates a proton to the alkoxide ion.
So water is a stronger acid than ethanol, and R is true.
The weaker the acid, the stronger its conjugate base. Hence C2H5O⁻ is a better proton acceptor than OH⁻, and A is true.
R directly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Treatment of $CH_3–CH=CH–CH_2OH$ with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) gives $CH_3–CH=CH–CHO$ in good yield.
Statement II: Tertiary alcohols are readily oxidised by $CrO_3$ to ketones having the same number of carbon atoms.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. PCC is a complex of $CrO_3$ with pyridine and HCl. It oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes in good yield, and NCERT gives exactly this example: but-2-en-1-ol to but-2-enal.
Statement II is false. Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation under normal conditions.
With strong oxidants and heat, tertiary alcohols undergo C–C cleavage and give acids with fewer carbon atoms, not ketones with the same number.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about acidity is INCORRECT?
options: Alcohols are weaker acids than water
Sodium ethoxide is a stronger base than sodium hydroxide
m-Nitrophenol is a stronger acid than p-nitrophenol
Cresols are weaker acids than phenol
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: water protonates an alkoxide ion, so water is the better proton donor.
(2) Correct: alkoxide ions accept protons more readily than $OH^-$.
(3) Incorrect: the pKa of m-nitrophenol is 8.3 and that of p-nitrophenol is 7.1, so the para isomer is the stronger acid. A –$NO_2$ group at the para position delocalises the phenoxide charge effectively; at the meta position it cannot.
(4) Correct: the electron-releasing $CH_3$ group lowers acidity (cresol pKa about 10.1–10.2, phenol 10.0).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the mechanism of acid-catalysed hydration of an alkene is INCORRECT?
options: In the first step, the alkene is protonated by electrophilic attack of $H_3O^+$ to form a carbocation.
In the second step, a water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbocation.
In the final step, the protonated alcohol loses a proton to give the alcohol.
The acid is consumed in the reaction and is not regenerated, so it acts as a reagent rather than a catalyst.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Step 1 is the electrophilic attack of H$_3$O$^+$ on the alkene, which forms a carbocation.
(2) Correct: Step 2 is the nucleophilic attack of H$_2$O on the carbocation, giving a protonated alcohol.
(3) Correct: Step 3 is deprotonation of the protonated alcohol to give the alcohol.
(4) Incorrect: the proton released in step 3 regenerates the acid. That is why the acid acts as a catalyst and is not consumed.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol can be separated by steam distillation, with o-nitrophenol distilling over.
Reason (R): o-Nitrophenol shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas p-nitrophenol shows intermolecular hydrogen bonding that associates its molecules.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: o-nitrophenol is steam volatile, so it can be separated from the para isomer by steam distillation.
R is true: in o-nitrophenol the –OH and –NO$_2$ groups are adjacent and form a hydrogen bond within the same molecule. The para isomer forms hydrogen bonds between molecules.
Intermolecular association lowers the volatility of p-nitrophenol, while the ortho isomer stays unassociated and volatile. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pKa values of phenol and ethanol are 10.0 and 15.9, respectively. By roughly what factor is the acid dissociation constant ($K_a$) of phenol greater than that of ethanol?
questions.explanation:
Given: pKa(phenol) = 10.0 and pKa(ethanol) = 15.9.
Formula: $K_a = 10^{-pK_a}$, so $\frac{K_a(\text{phenol})}{K_a(\text{ethanol})} = 10^{(15.9 - 10.0)}$.
Substituting: $10^{5.9} \approx 7.9 \times 10^{5}$.
So phenol is close to a million times more acidic than ethanol, as NCERT states.
The option 5.9 is only the difference in pKa values. It is not the ratio of the $K_a$ values.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the reaction of ethers with HI is INCORRECT?
options: (CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–CH$_3$ with HI gives (CH$_3$)$_3$C–I and CH$_3$OH, through an S$_N$1 pathway
CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$–O–CH$_3$ with HI gives CH$_3$I and propan-1-ol, because I$^-$ attacks the less substituted carbon by S$_N$2
Ethoxyethane with excess HI at high temperature finally gives two molecules of ethyl iodide
Anisole with excess HI at high temperature finally gives iodobenzene and methyl iodide
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: loss of CH$_3$OH from the protonated ether leaves the stable (CH$_3$)$_3$C$^+$ ion, which I$^-$ then traps.
(2) Correct: with primary and secondary alkyl groups, the lower alkyl group becomes the alkyl iodide.
(3) Correct: the ethanol formed reacts with more HI to give C$_2$H$_5$I.
(4) Incorrect: anisole gives phenol and CH$_3$I. Phenol is not converted to iodobenzene, because its sp$^2$ carbon cannot undergo nucleophilic substitution.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Vapours of 2-methylpropan-2-ol are passed over heated copper at 573 K. The main product is:
questions.explanation:
Primary alcohols undergo dehydrogenation over Cu at 573 K to give aldehydes. Secondary alcohols give ketones the same way.
Tertiary alcohols have no H on the carbinol carbon, so dehydrogenation cannot occur. Instead they undergo dehydration.
$(CH_3)_3COH$ therefore loses water to give $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$, which is 2-methylpropene.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol is steam distilled, o-nitrophenol distils over.
Reason (R): o-Nitrophenol shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas p-nitrophenol molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile, so it is separated from the para isomer by steam distillation.
R is true. In the ortho isomer, the –OH and –$NO_2$ groups are adjacent and hydrogen bond within the same molecule. The para isomer forms hydrogen bonds between molecules, which associates them and makes the compound less volatile.
R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Methylmagnesium bromide is treated with methanal, and the adduct is then hydrolysed. The organic product is:
questions.explanation:
The Grignard reagent adds to the C=O group. The $CH_3^-$ part bonds to the carbonyl carbon and the MgBr part bonds to oxygen.
Adduct: $CH_3CH_2OMgBr$. Hydrolysis then gives $CH_3CH_2OH$.
NCERT: methanal gives a primary alcohol, other aldehydes give secondary alcohols and ketones give tertiary alcohols.
Propan-2-ol would need ethanal as the carbonyl compound. Methanol would mean no new C–C bond had formed.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol, methoxymethane and propane have comparable molecular masses. Which of the following correctly shows their boiling points in decreasing order?
questions.explanation:
Ethanol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so it has the highest boiling point.
Methoxymethane has polar C–O bonds and a net dipole moment, but no O–H bond. Its molecules cannot hydrogen bond with each other, so its boiling point is intermediate.
Propane is non-polar and has only weak van der Waals forces, so it has the lowest boiling point.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction of phenol) with List-II (main product):
List-I
(A) Reimer–Tiemann reaction
(B) Kolbe's reaction
(C) Heating with zinc dust
(D) Oxidation with chromic acid
List-II
(i) Benzene
(ii) Benzoquinone
(iii) Salicylaldehyde
(iv) o-Hydroxybenzoic acid
questions.explanation:
(A) Reimer–Tiemann: phenol reacts with CHCl$_3$ and NaOH. A –CHO group enters the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde (iii).
(B) Kolbe: the phenoxide ion reacts with CO$_2$ to give o-hydroxybenzoic acid (iv).
(C) Heating phenol with zinc dust gives benzene (i).
(D) Chromic acid oxidises phenol to benzoquinone, a conjugated diketone (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (common name) with List-II (IUPAC name):
List-I
(A) Catechol
(B) Resorcinol
(C) Hydroquinone
(D) Glycerol
List-II
(I) Benzene-1,4-diol
(II) Propane-1,2,3-triol
(III) Benzene-1,2-diol
(IV) Benzene-1,3-diol
questions.explanation:
(A) Catechol has its two –OH groups ortho to each other, so it is benzene-1,2-diol (III).
(B) Resorcinol has them meta, so it is benzene-1,3-diol (IV).
(C) Hydroquinone (quinol) has them para, so it is benzene-1,4-diol (I).
(D) Glycerol has three –OH groups on a propane chain, so it is propane-1,2,3-triol (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (ether + reagent/conditions) with List-II (products):
List-I
(A) C$_6$H$_5$–O–CH$_3$ + HI
(B) (CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–C$_2$H$_5$ + HI
(C) CH$_3$–O–CH$_2$CH$_2$CH$_3$ + HI (one equivalent)
(D) C$_2$H$_5$–O–C$_2$H$_5$ + excess HI, high temperature
List-II
(I) CH$_3$I + CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH
(II) 2 C$_2$H$_5$I + H$_2$O
(III) C$_6$H$_5$OH + CH$_3$I
(IV) (CH$_3$)$_3$C–I + C$_2$H$_5$OH
questions.explanation:
(A) The aryl–O bond is stronger, so the products are phenol and CH$_3$I (III).
(B) The tert-alkyl group gives a stable carbocation, so the reaction is S$_N$1 and gives tert-butyl iodide and ethanol (IV).
(C) With primary groups the reaction is S$_N$2. I$^-$ attacks the less substituted CH$_3$, giving CH$_3$I and propan-1-ol (I).
(D) With excess HI, the ethanol formed first is also converted, so two molecules of C$_2$H$_5$I form along with water (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following reactions give the indicated ether as the major product?
(i) $CH_3ONa + (CH_3)_3C–Br$ → tert-butyl methyl ether
(ii) $(CH_3)_3C–ONa + CH_3Br$ → tert-butyl methyl ether
(iii) $C_6H_5ONa + CH_3Br$ → methoxybenzene
(iv) $CH_3ONa + C_6H_5Br$ → methoxybenzene
(v) Ethanol + conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 413 K → ethoxyethane
(vi) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol + conc. $H_2SO_4$, heat → di-tert-butyl ether
questions.explanation:
(i) No. The alkoxide acts as a strong base on the 3° halide, so elimination occurs and 2-methylpropene is the only product.
(ii) Yes. This is SN2 attack of the bulky alkoxide on unhindered CH3Br.
(iii) Yes. Phenoxide attacks the 1° (methyl) halide.
(iv) No. The sp2 carbon of an aryl halide does not undergo SN2 substitution.
(v) Yes. This is bimolecular dehydration of a 1° unhindered alcohol at low temperature.
(vi) No. Elimination dominates for 3° alcohols, so an alkene forms.
Three reactions are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following symmetrical ethers can be prepared satisfactorily by bimolecular acid dehydration (conc. $H_2SO_4$) of the corresponding alcohol?
Ethoxyethane, 1-propoxypropane, 1-butoxybutane, 2-isopropoxypropane (diisopropyl ether), di-tert-butyl ether
questions.explanation:
Acid dehydration to give an ether suits only unhindered primary alcohols kept at a low temperature, because it is an SN2 attack of an alcohol on a protonated alcohol.
Ethoxyethane (from ethanol), 1-propoxypropane (from propan-1-ol) and 1-butoxybutane (from butan-1-ol) come from primary alcohols. Suitable.
Diisopropyl ether (from a 2° alcohol) and di-tert-butyl ether (from a 3° alcohol) cannot be made this way: elimination wins and alkenes form.
So 3 of the ethers qualify.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Invertase
(B) Zymase
(C) ZnO–Cr$_2$O$_3$
(D) Pyridine
List-II
(i) Hydrogenation of CO to methanol
(ii) Foul-smelling denaturant of ethanol
(iii) Conversion of sugar to glucose and fructose
(iv) Conversion of glucose to ethanol and CO$_2$
questions.explanation:
(A) Invertase hydrolyses cane sugar to glucose and fructose → (iii).
(B) Zymase, present in yeast, ferments glucose and fructose to ethanol and CO$_2$ → (iv).
(C) ZnO–Cr$_2$O$_3$ catalyses the hydrogenation of CO to methanol → (i).
(D) Pyridine is the foul-smelling liquid used to denature alcohol → (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the esterification of an alcohol with an acid chloride, $R'COCl$, the reaction is carried out in the presence of pyridine. What is the main role of pyridine?
options: It acts as a dehydrating agent that removes water formed in the reaction
It neutralises the HCl formed and shifts the equilibrium towards the ester
It oxidises the alcohol to an aldehyde before esterification
It acts as a Lewis acid that polarises the C=O bond of the acid chloride
questions.explanation:
The reaction is $ROH + R'COCl \rightarrow ROCOR' + HCl$.
Pyridine is a base. It neutralises the HCl as it forms, which shifts the equilibrium to the right.
Removing water is the strategy used with carboxylic acids and conc. $H_2SO_4$. No water is formed here, so option (1) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The boiling point of ethoxyethane (307.6 K) is very close to that of n-pentane (309.1 K), which has a comparable molecular mass.
Reason (R): The C–O bonds in ethers are non-polar, so ethers have zero net dipole moment.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT gives 307.6 K for ethoxyethane and 309.1 K for n-pentane, so their boiling points are comparable.
R is false. The C–O bonds in ethers are polar, and ethers do have a net dipole moment because the C–O–C unit is bent.
The correct reason for A is different. The polarity of ethers is weak and does not appreciably raise the boiling point. Ether molecules also cannot hydrogen bond with one another.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Commercially, carboxylic acids are converted to alcohols by first forming their esters and then hydrogenating the esters catalytically, rather than by direct reduction with LiAlH$_4$.
Reason (R): Lithium aluminium hydride is an expensive reagent, so it is used only for preparing special chemicals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that, commercially, acids are esterified and the esters are reduced with H$_2$ in the presence of a catalyst.
R is true: LiAlH$_4$ reduces acids to primary alcohols very efficiently, but it is costly. It is therefore reserved for preparing special chemicals.
The high cost of LiAlH$_4$ is exactly why industry prefers the cheaper ester-hydrogenation route. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following give a primary alcohol as the main product?
(i) Reduction of $RCOOH$ with $LiAlH_4$ followed by water
(ii) Catalytic hydrogenation of butanal
(iii) Methanal + $RMgX$, followed by hydrolysis
(iv) Propanone + $CH_3MgBr$, followed by hydrolysis
(v) Reduction of butan-2-one with $NaBH_4$
(vi) Hydroboration–oxidation of propene
questions.explanation:
(i) Primary: $LiAlH_4$ reduces the acid to $RCH_2OH$.
(ii) Primary: aldehydes reduce to primary alcohols, so butanal gives butan-1-ol.
(iii) Primary: methanal with a Grignard reagent gives a primary alcohol.
(iv) Not primary: a ketone with a Grignard reagent gives a tertiary alcohol (2-methylpropan-2-ol).
(v) Not primary: a ketone reduces to a secondary alcohol (butan-2-ol).
(vi) Primary: boron adds to the carbon carrying more H atoms, so propan-1-ol forms.
Four reactions give a primary alcohol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An ether X of molecular formula C$_5$H$_{12}$O, on heating with one equivalent of HI, gives 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol. Identify X and the mechanism of the C–O bond cleavage.
questions.explanation:
The products show that X contains a tert-butyl group and a methyl group on the oxygen. X is therefore (CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–CH$_3$, 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane, which fits C$_5$H$_{12}$O.
If the mechanism were S$_N$2, I$^-$ would attack the less substituted CH$_3$ and give CH$_3$I. That is not what is observed.
Instead, the protonated ether loses CH$_3$OH to give the stable (CH$_3$)$_3$C$^+$, which then captures I$^-$. This is the S$_N$1 pathway.
1-Methoxy-2-methylpropane would give CH$_3$I and 2-methylpropan-1-ol. 2-Ethoxypropane would give C$_2$H$_5$I and propan-2-ol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following give a primary alcohol as the major organic product?
(i) Ethanoic acid treated with $LiAlH_4$, then $H_2O$
(ii) Propanone treated with $NaBH_4$
(iii) But-1-ene treated with $B_2H_6$, then $H_2O_2$/NaOH
(iv) But-1-ene treated with water in the presence of dilute $H_2SO_4$
(v) $CH_3MgBr$ with methanal, followed by hydrolysis
(vi) $C_2H_5MgBr$ with ethanal, followed by hydrolysis
(vii) Ethyl ethanoate treated with $H_2$ in the presence of a catalyst
questions.explanation:
(i) Primary: $LiAlH_4$ reduces the acid to ethanol.
(ii) Not primary: a ketone gives a 2° alcohol, propan-2-ol.
(iii) Primary: the anti-Markovnikov product is butan-1-ol.
(iv) Not primary: the Markovnikov product is butan-2-ol (2°).
(v) Primary: methanal gives ethanol.
(vi) Not primary: an aldehyde other than HCHO gives a 2° alcohol, butan-2-ol.
(vii) Primary: catalytic hydrogenation of the ester gives ethanol.
Primary alcohol is formed in (i), (iii), (v) and (vii), so the count is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Anisole is treated with ethanoyl chloride (CH$_3$COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl$_3$. The major product P is isolated and then heated with excess concentrated HI. The final organic products are:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Friedel–Crafts acylation of anisole introduces the CH$_3$CO group at the ortho and para positions. The para product, 4-methoxyacetophenone, is P.
Step 2: HI cleaves P at the alkyl–O bond, because the aryl–O bond has partial double bond character.
This gives CH$_3$I and 4-hydroxyacetophenone.
The aryl C–O bond is not replaced by iodine, so 4-iodoacetophenone is not formed. The meta product is ruled out because the –OCH$_3$ group is ortho/para directing.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In Kolbe's reaction, phenol is first treated with sodium hydroxide before being allowed to react with carbon dioxide. The main reason for this step is that:
options: NaOH converts $CO_2$ into a strong electrophile, $CO_3^{2-}$
NaOH deactivates the ring so that only monosubstitution occurs
The phenoxide ion is more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic substitution, and $CO_2$ is only a weak electrophile
Phenol itself is meta-directing, while phenoxide is ortho-directing
questions.explanation:
Phenoxide ion carries a full negative charge on oxygen. This makes the ring even more electron rich than in phenol.
$CO_2$ is a weak electrophile, so it can attack only this highly activated ring.
The main product is ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).
Option (4) fails because phenol is already ortho/para directing.
Option (1) fails because $CO_3^{2-}$ is not an electrophile.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following compounds is the –OH group bonded to an sp$^2$ hybridised carbon of a carbon–carbon double bond (a vinylic alcohol)?
questions.explanation:
In a vinylic alcohol the –OH group is attached directly to a doubly bonded (sp$^2$) carbon, giving a C$_{sp^2}$–OH bond.
(a) CH$_2$=CH–OH: the –OH is on a C=C carbon, so it is vinylic.
(b) The –OH is on an sp$^3$ carbon next to the C=C, so this is an allylic alcohol. This is the tempting distractor.
(c) The –OH is on an sp$^3$ carbon next to the ring, so this is benzylic.
(d) This is a tertiary alcohol with a C$_{sp^3}$–OH bond.
Answer: (a)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) Methanol (b.p. 337 K) boils at a lower temperature than ethanol (b.p. 351 K).
(b) Methanol is used chiefly for making formaldehyde.
(c) Zymase keeps fermenting sugar however high the alcohol concentration becomes.
(d) Carbon dioxide is released during fermentation of sugars.
(e) Large quantities of ethanol are nowadays obtained by hydration of ethene.
(f) Most methanol today is produced by destructive distillation of wood.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: methanol boils at 337 K and ethanol at 351 K.
(b) Correct: methanol is used as a solvent and chiefly for making formaldehyde.
(c) Incorrect: zymase is inhibited once the alcohol content exceeds about 14%.
(d) Correct: CO$_2$ is evolved during fermentation.
(e) Correct: hydration of ethene now supplies large quantities of ethanol.
(f) Incorrect: destructive distillation of wood was the old method. Most methanol now comes from CO + H$_2$ over ZnO–Cr$_2$O$_3$.
There are 4 correct statements.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Glucose is fermented by zymase according to $C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2$. If 360 g of glucose is fermented with 80% yield, what mass of ethanol is obtained? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation:
Given: 360 g glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol); yield 80%; molar mass of ethanol 46 g/mol.
Formula: moles of ethanol = 2 × moles of glucose × yield fraction.
Substituting: moles of glucose = 360/180 = 2 mol, so theoretical ethanol = 4 mol.
Actual ethanol = 0.80 × 4 = 3.2 mol, and mass = 3.2 × 46 = 147.2 g.
184 g is the answer if the 80% yield is ignored.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sodium methoxide ($CH_3ONa$) is treated with tert-butyl bromide, $(CH_3)_3C-Br$. What is the product?
questions.explanation:
Alkoxides are strong nucleophiles, but they are also strong bases.
With a tertiary alkyl halide, back-side SN2 attack is blocked, so the methoxide removes a β-hydrogen instead (elimination).
NCERT states that this reaction gives 2-methylpropene exclusively, and no ether is formed.
The expected ether, 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane, therefore does not form by this route.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following reactions give a primary alcohol as the main product?
(i) Hydroboration–oxidation of propene
(ii) Acid-catalysed hydration of propene
(iii) Butanoic acid treated with LiAlH$_4$, then H$_2$O
(iv) Propanone reduced with NaBH$_4$
(v) CH$_3$MgBr with methanal, then hydrolysis
(vi) C$_2$H$_5$MgBr with ethanal, then hydrolysis
(vii) Catalytic hydrogenation of butanal
questions.explanation:
(i) Primary: boron adds to CH$_2$, giving propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov product).
(ii) Not primary: Markovnikov addition gives propan-2-ol.
(iii) Primary: LiAlH$_4$ reduces the acid to butan-1-ol.
(iv) Not primary: a ketone gives a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol.
(v) Primary: methanal gives ethanol.
(vi) Not primary: an aldehyde other than methanal gives a secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol.
(vii) Primary: an aldehyde is reduced to butan-1-ol.
So 4 reactions give primary alcohols.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 7 · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Using the pKa data given in NCERT, which of the following compounds is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation:
A lower pKa means a stronger acid.
The pKa values are: p-nitrophenol 7.1, o-nitrophenol 7.2, m-nitrophenol 8.3 and phenol 10.0.
p-Nitrophenol has the lowest value, so it is the strongest acid.
o-Nitrophenol is very close (7.2) but is still slightly weaker.
Answer: (3)
